Industry News: SPORT E SALUTE E ADIDAS, CONTRO IL DROP-OUT ZACCAGNI PORTA IN CLASSE LA VOGLIA DI NON MOLLARE MAI

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Roma, il capitano della Lazio incontra gli alunni della scuola primaria Pistelli vincitrice del contest nazionale “AttiviAMOci tutti i giorni in movimento”.
  • ROMA – Gol al novantesimo o weekend senza compiti?
  • CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Roma, il capitano della Lazio incontra gli alunni della scuola primaria Pistelli vincitrice del contest nazionale “AttiviAMOci tutti i giorni in movimento”. Tra gioco, movimento e storie personali, un messaggio: nello sport, come nella vita, la ver.

ROMA – Gol al novantesimo o weekend senza compiti? Derby vinto o 10 in matematica? Questa volta la sfida si gioca tra i banchi di scuola e a scendere in campo è Mattia Zaccagni. Il capitano della Lazio incontra i bambini della Scuola Primaria Pistelli di Roma per una partita speciale a colpi di “Questo o quello?”, tra domande a sorpresa, risposte istintive e qualche scelta davvero difficile.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

L’appuntamento fa parte del percorso nazionale promosso da Sport e Salute e adidas per contrastare il drop-out sportivo e tenere viva, fin dai primi anni, la voglia di fare sport. E la Pistelli non è una scuola qualsiasi: istituto aderente a Scuola Attiva Kids, è stata protagonista del contest nazionale “AttiviAMOci tutti i giorni in movimento”, conquistando il primo posto grazie al percorso realizzato per promuovere il movimento come parte integrante della quotidianità scolastica. Una comunità che ha scelto di fare dello sport un’abitudine, un’opportunità e un’esperienza da condividere.

In a recent development, È proprio da questa energia che prende vita l’incontro con Zaccagni. I bambini diventano arbitri delle scelte, mentre il campione si mette alla prova: gol decisivo o vacanza più lunga? Una partita vinta o un bel voto a scuola? Ma dietro le risate e le risposte più divertenti c’è anche spazio per qualcosa di più profondo. Perché lo sport non è soltanto il momento della vittoria: è imparare a gestire una sconfitta, superare un errore, affrontare una difficoltà e trovare ogni volta la voglia di ripartire.

«Nel calcio, come nella vita, ci sono momenti in cui le cose non vanno come vorresti. Puoi sbagliare un gol, perdere una partita o attraversare un periodo complicato. Ma è proprio in quei momenti che devi trovare la forza di rialzarti, continuare a lavorare e credere nelle tue capacità. Io ho imparato che non si cresce soltanto quando si vince, ma soprattutto quando si riesce a reagire alle difficoltà. Ai ragazzi dico di divertirsi, di non avere paura di sbagliare e di non mollare mai quello che li fa stare bene. Perché nello sport, prima ancora dei risultati, conta la voglia di continuare a giocare», racconta Mattia Zaccagni ai bambini.

Dalle parole si passa al movimento. Con i tutor di Sport e Salute, gli alunni partecipano a una lezione di attività motoria, tra giochi, prove di abilità e lavoro di squadra. Tutti protagonisti, ciascuno con le proprie capacità, in un’esperienza che mette al centro il piacere di muoversi e stare insieme.

È questa la sfida che Sport e Salute e adidas vogliono vincere: contrastare l’abbandono sportivo, offrendo ai più giovani occasioni per scoprire una passione, sentirsi parte di una squadra e trovare nello sport uno spazio in cui crescere. Perché nessuno dovrebbe smettere di giocare solo perché non è il più bravo, perché ha incontrato una difficoltà o perché una partita è andata male.

La Pistelli, con il suo percorso premiato a livello nazionale, dimostra che questa partita può iniziare proprio dalla scuola. E che il risultato più importante non è segnare un gol in più, ma fare in modo che domani ci siano ancora tanti bambini pronti a scendere in campo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the eve of AC Milan’s game against Frosinone, Ruben Amorim spoke to the media at the usual pre-match press conference.

The international break is officially over and Milan will be back in action tomorrow. After wins against Inter and Genoa, the goal is to make it three consecutive wins, although an in-form Frosinone side will be looking to make life difficult for them.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amorim’s initiative appears to be to field an attacking-minded starting eleven, picking up where he left off against Genoa. It’s certainly a bold plan as Frosinone will surely look to cause complications on the counter, as also highlighted by Oliver in his prediction.

Speaking to the media at Milanello, Amorim shared his thoughts on the game, the status of the players after the international break, and the tactical solutions moving forward.

“We as a club have a substantial responsibility. Fondazione Milan is really key because it reflects our values and helps the community. Our doors are always open for everyone. It’s also good for the players to see and live different realities.”.

On those involved in international duty….

“I think everyone is ready. Of course, we had to control the load during the week, because some of them travelled a lot. I’m really pleased with our players getting game time, because that’s the best way to maintain, so we are ready for the game.”.

On Pavlovic’s status and Frosinone’s style..

Recent findings suggest that “Starting with Pavlovic, he’s doing better. He will be in the squad. I don’t know if he will start or not, so I will see. He wants to play and I want him to play. We miss that fire that he has. Let’s see, but for sure he will be in the team.

“Frosinone are fun to watch, they are the team that runs the most, and we are second so I think we can fight that. They are really good with 1v1s on the flanks. If you watch their games it’s hard to understand their movement. There is some logic in their chaos, but it’s hard to spot.

It has been revealed that “They play a different style, more direct, which allows them to have the ball more inside the box. So it’s going to be a really hard game. As I remarked against Venezia, there are some teams that we need to be really focused against because their styles can cause complications.”.

In a recent development, camarda is getting little game time, despite the Ramos struggles. Is a strong deputy striker missing?

In a recent development, “Two different questions. Of course we can say that one more option would be a good thing, but I think the struggles of Ramos are the struggles of the team. We are not reaching the final third, we are one of the worst teams in that sense. So we don’t have a lot of shots.

“I don’t want loads of shots outside the box, because it’s hard to score with those. We need to get into the box and we are not helping Ramos. What I saw against Genoa is that without Ramos, we wouldn’t have scored those goals. But again, we need to do better in the final third, my goal is to push the team forward. That’s my job.

“It’s true that he’s working hard and doing a lot of good. I know that it’s not his sole job to press, we spent a lot of money on a player to score goals, but we are not doing enough to help him. We need to push the team forward.”.

Are you happy with the league standings so far? And against Genoa, you basically played with four attacking players. Can this be a solution for the future?

Industry observers note that “Starting with the last question, it depends on the opponents and the moment of the team. I don’t believe that playing with more attackers means you will reach the final third more. Sometimes you get that effect from having more midfielders, for example. We are always going to change in some matches depending on the opponent.

“On the first question, it’s difficult to say. I think that we have grown as a team quite fast, but I’m not pleased with the overall situation. We need to be so much better and as such, I’m not pleased with where we are in the standings. But of course, I need to say that I’m happy with how the players have worked.”.

According to recent reports, during the break, we saw Camarda scoring for the U21s. Could a loan be the right solution?

Recent findings suggest that “I was a young player myself once too. A young player wants everything really badly, which is a good thing. That said, he needs time to adapt, it’s really hard to play for a club like Milan. You just said there is pressure on Ramos, imagine what it’s like for Camarda.

“I don’t know what will happen in January, but he needs to be focused on these games. Everything can change in just a few weeks.

It has been revealed that “I’m really happy with how he has been since he returned from international duty, I heard that Baldini spoke with him at length (as Baldini remarked himself), and he returned in a happier mood. I understand the question about January, but January is so far away right now.”.

The feeling is that the team is struggling to keep control at the end of the games….

“Sometimes even when we are winning, we have dropped the levels in every action of the game. I think we are controlling everything better, you saw it in the second half against Genoa without spending a lot of energy, but I think it’s all connected to the attack.

“If we don’t create danger when we are leading, we will struggle a bit to kill the games. Of course, we need to address that and we are working on it.”.

On Musah as a left-back and if more versatile players will be signed….

Industry observers note that “That was a specific situation. I don’t know and I’m not going to tell you guys what we are thinking about January. I wanted a right-footed player against Genoa. You saw the runs of Rabiot, so I wanted someone right-footed to pass the ball on immediately.

It has been revealed that “Musah is not going to play as a left-back tomorrow, I can tell you that, but it’s an option. I like to have players who can play in several positions.”.

“I think it helps any player to feel the confidence from the club. I think it’s clear that was done with the new contract. Then I also told you when he wasn’t playing that he’s really key for us. I can tell you today that Pulisic perhaps is the one player we cannot replace.

“The movement in between the lines he brings, we simply don’t have another Pulisic. His absence is always felt a lot, so from that you can understand how vital he is for us. He doesn’t talk a lot, but he lets the pitch do the talking.

Sources indicate that “I would put him in the same category as Rabiot. Players who are on another level. I don’t like speaking about individuals, but I think everyone can see this.”.

Can the January transfer window serve to raise the team’s ambition?

In a recent development, “That is the biggest mistake of the significant clubs. Looking at the table and deciding whether to invest or not. I think the key is to have a long-term plan. Stick with your plan. We have one and everything is very clear.

“Trying to become a champion by spending money is the biggest mistake. The key is following your proposal. I look at the table to evaluate the process as a whole, not to decide whether to spend a lot on signings.”.

Are you keeping track of your players so they don’t stay up late at night playing GTA?

“I will let my friend Gennaro Gattuso respond. Jokes aside, I don’t care.”.

Recent findings suggest that is a winner a dreamer who never gives up? Are you a dreamer?

Recent findings suggest that “I wouldn’t call it a dream but the goal is to win every game. If you look at my journey, every club I chose, I clearly am a dreamer [laughs]. I really want to be part of this club for the rest of my career, but I also know that I need to prove myself.

“I’m a dreamer, yes, but also very focused on the goal.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il Torino festeggerà i 120 anni di storia il prossimo 3 dicembre, con un allenamento a porte aperte allo stadio Olimpico organizzato dalla società granata, ma anche con una speciale divisa da gioco pensata per l'occasione. Lo ha fatto sapere la società granata: "Nella stagione del 120º anniversario del Club, Torino FC e Joma presentano una maglia speciale per la stagione 2026/27: un'edizione celebrativa che riprende alcuni segni dell'identità granata con uno sguardo rivolto al presente e all’innovazione".

1906 – 2026 🫀🐂 https://t.co/DmYnS3IwB5— Torino Football Club (@TorinoFC_1906) November 25, 2026.

1906 – 2026 🫀🐂 https://t.co/DmYnS3IwB5.

Industry observers note that il club rende noto anche quando sarà impiegato: "La maglia celebrativa farà il suo esordio al Grande Torino sabato 28 novembre alle 18:00, in occasione di Torino-Lazio e darà il via alle iniziative che accompagneranno il Club fino a giovedì 3 dicembre e oltre. Dal Filadelfia allo stadio, dagli anni Ottanta a oggi: questa maglia non chiede di guardare indietro, ma di celebrare le nostre radici nel presente. Ci ricorda che la Storia e la tradizione del Toro vivranno per sempre, grazie a chi continua a indossare questo colore e a tenere accesa la fede Granata".

It has been revealed that il comunicato racconta anche le principali caratteristiche della nuova divisa: "Una maglia pensata per essere unica in ogni suo esemplare: l'edizione è limitata a soli 1906 pezzi, come l'anno di fondazione del Club, ciascuno con il proprio numero seriale sul fronte. La trama del tessuto, composta da sottili linee bianche adagiate sullo storico granata acceso, riprende quella di una maglia da allenamento utilizzata negli anni ‘80: un capo nato per il lavoro quotidiano al Filadelfia, dove con fatica e sudore si preparava la partita del weekend. Oggi quella stessa trama lascia il campo d'allenamento ed è pronta a vivere una nuova vita, reinterpretata con un linguaggio contemporaneo. Sulla maglia campeggia il toro rampante degli anni Ottanta: un simbolo tramandato dai racconti e dalla passione di nonni e genitori, che unisce generazioni diverse di tifosi, da chi lo conosce da sempre a chi ha iniziato a indossarlo da poco. A celebrare l'anniversario c'è una patch dorata dall'effetto cangiante. A seconda della luce e del punto di vista, la scritta “Edizione limitata”, il logo e il numero 120 lasciano spazio al numero seriale del singolo esemplare. Ogni dettaglio racconta i 120 anni del Club. Lo stemma con il toro rampante è ricamato sul petto all'altezza del cuore, mentre i bordi delle maniche sono realizzati in un tessuto elastico a coste, sul quale ricompare il 120. All’interno del colletto è stampata la data di nascita del Club: 3 dicembre 1906. Il tessuto è leggerissimo e lavorato per far respirare la pelle, così da lasciare ai giocatori la massima libertà di movimento. È realizzato interamente in poliestere riciclato, ottenuto da bottiglie di plastica: un materiale resistente e di qualità, rispetto ai tessuti tradizionali. Nelle zone in cui si suda di più, una sottile rete traforata aiuta la maglia ad asciugarsi più in fretta. Le cuciture sono robuste ma non danno fastidio, mentre colletto e polsini elastici fanno aderire bene la maglia al corpo, senza stringere".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Le dichiarazioni dell'ex team manager della Lazio sul cammino in campionato.

Compleanno dolce per Maurizio Manzini, storico team manager della Lazio, intervenuto a Radiosei durante ‘NMM‘  per commentare il momento positivo dei biancocelesti.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, questo mio compleanno lo festeggio in un momento piacevole dal punto di vista sportivo. È orgoglio vedere la Lazio lì in classifica, grazie al lavoro di Rino e della squadra. È un grande merito loro ed una grande soddisfazione per noi. Come andrà a finire la stagione? Non lo dico per scaramanzia, diciamo che speriamo di salvarci.

In a recent development, il legame tra Maurizio Manzini e il club capitolino nasce da lontano, già nel 1971, quando da dirigente nel settore dell'aviazione iniziò a supportare volontariamente la società nella gestione logistica e delle trasferte, conquistando la stima di figure leggendarie come Tommaso Maestrelli. Dopo un primo rifiuto, nella stagione 1988/89 accettò ufficialmente l'incarico di team manager, diventando per decenni l'anello di congiunzione indispensabile tra spogliatoio e vertici societari. Poliglotta, apprezzato da arbitri, colleghi e persino dagli avversari per stile e riservatezza, ha rappresentato la memoria storica del club fino al graduale passaggio di consegne avvenuto a partire dall'annata 2014/15.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Francesco Camarda could join Cagliari on loan in January and as part of the deal, AC Milan could obtain an option for Paul Mendy, according to a report.

There has been a lot of speculation regarding Camarda’s future in the last few weeks. The 18-year-old has played just 119 minutes so far this season and it’s clear that his development isn’t moving in the right direction as a result.

A loan seems to be the most likely option, especially if Milan were to bring in another striker, but the substantial question is where he should go. After a so-so loan spell at Lecce, the Rossoneri must evaluate carefully before making their choice.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, Cagliari have expressed a concrete interest in securing Camarda on a loan with an option to buy, leaving a buy-back in favour of Milan. In other words, it would be the same formula that was used when he moved to Lecce.

There is one big difference, though. As per the journalist, the Cagliari striker Paul Mendy could also be involved in the deal. The idea would be to add a ‘buy option’ for Milan, presumably giving them priority to sign the player for a pre-agreed fee.

The 19-year-old has bagged two goals and two assists for the Sardinian side so far, attracting the interest of several clubs (and not just Milan).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers head to managerless Watford tonight as they look to move into the Championship’s top half with a win. Under the temporary lead of Damien Johnson, the East Lancashire outfit come into the game in 13th after a 2-2 draw with rivals Burnley on Sunday.

The Hornets had hoped Edward Iordanescu would be in charge for the game, but with no confirmation of his appointment as of Wednesday morning, they look set to be led by an interim team fronted by Adrian Mariappa. It marks a tough test for the hosts, as Rovers have a string of dangerous attackers in their arsenal.

Rovers’ impressing attackers and Watford’s struggles at the back could see the away side take all three points back to Ewood Park with them.

First of all, we’ll look at the numbers behind Watford’s struggling defence.

Industry observers note that the Hornets have conceded 28.5 xG, ranking them 19th in the Championship (FotMob). Their actual goals-conceded tally sits at 27, and the consensus at Vicarage Road is that they would be a lot worse off if it weren’t for impressing goalkeeper Federico Ravaglia.

They have faced 256 shots this season, which averages out at 16 per game. This, combined with their xG conceded, goes to show just how many shooting opportunities Watford afford their opposition, and it will set Blackburn Rovers tongues wagging.

In Andri Gudjohnsen, the visitors have one of the most clinical strikers in Europe. His 11 Championship goals from 24 shots equate to a 45.83% conversion rate, and in the continent’s top five leagues, the only strikers who can better that are Stade Rennais’ Boulaye Dia (60%) and Carlos Espi of Real Madrid (50% – via FBref).

If Watford concede chances like they have been this season, Gudjohnsen will get on the scoresheet.

Second-top scorer Oladapo Afolayan will be one to watch because of this too. Not only has he scored five league goals, but he’s contributed two assists as well. Captain and creative maestro Todd Cantwell will be at the centre of all attacks, and he should hope to add to his assist tally.

Depending on how much he is able to play after his recent return from injury, Ryoya Morishita is one to watch for the away side as well.

Sitting in 13th compared to Watford in 20th, Blackburn Rovers are favourites to win here. They’ve got the attacking talent to expose a poor Hornets defence.

However, there are caveats. The departure of Alessio Dionisi could bring the cliched ‘upcoming manager bounce’ for Watford, and under the interim lead of Mariappa, expect them to be motivated. His past as a defender and his previously leadership role in the dressing room at Vicarage Road could help tighten them up at the back.

But, with the attacking stars at their disposal, Rovers can win here and win comfortably if they’re on their game.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.
  • According to recent reports, in what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes.
  • City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

According to recent reports, in what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Industry observers note that could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

According to recent reports, the data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

Industry observers note that in the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz.

Sources indicate that it could have been a hat-trick. It could even have been four as Haaland, taking the captain’s armband as Rúben Dias was withdrawn during the interval, clipped the top of the crossbar with a header and then was denied by goalkeeper Matvei Safonov as the striker slid in.

“Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. Luis [Enrique, PSG’s coach] stated at the end of the game that they were quite lucky,” Maresca claimed before being asked whether he would relish facing PSG again, later in this competition. “My feeling is we are there. We are close,” he added.

Did City deserve a draw? No one was predicting that at half-time as they were suffering as comprehensive a defeat as was inflicted by the commission. Accused of “sham” contracts to inflate income, this was a sham of a performance, made all the more emphatic because of how brilliant PSG, and their exceptional 21-year-old winger Désiré Doué, were.

Désiré Doué with a brilliant finish from range to give PSG an early lead in Manchester 😮‍💨 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/Uwilx7I37H.

There is a certain irony that it was PSG who inflicted this defeat, ending City’s run of eight wins from eight in all competitions under Maresca.

It was a meeting of two clubs empowered more than any other by the riches of Gulf states: Abu Dhabi versus Qatar. Both have also had their run-ins over money. Both were sanctioned, but escaped full bans by Uefa for breaching financial fair play rules.

The question, also, was: would the eighth meeting of these clubs in the Champions League in the last 11 seasons be the last for some time?

It has been revealed that so we should savour it and we did. That included Pep Guardiola on his first return to the Etihad – in a sign of solidarity – after quitting at the end of last season. Not that he savoured much of what he saw as PSG dominated City to such an extent that their fans adopted the “Poznan” celebration and the home supporters were silenced.

City could have gone in front before they conceded with the erratic Safonov – who was Gianluigi Donnarumma’s understudy and has become his unlikely replacement – punching a corner against his own crossbar before Antoine Semenyo shot the rebound over.

In a recent development, then PSG ran all over City. They broke far too easily and scored far too easily. Not once, but twice, to go 2-0 up.

For the first, PSG countered, with City struggling to cover, and Doué caught out Donnarumma with a low shot inside his right-hand post from 22 yards.

Sources indicate that then PSG sliced through City’s defence with Ousmane Dembélé scooping the ball across the area to Doué who returned it back. Dembélé stooped to head home.

Ousmane Dembélé doubles PSG's lead just 2 minutes after they scored the first 🤯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/MxhJ3oCWpC.

After Achraf Hakimi headed against the inside of a post and City could not clear, the ball came back with Warren Zaïre-Emery flicking on Maghnes Akliouche’s cut-back. It ran to Vitinha who slammed in a first-time shot. It was the first time City had ever conceded three goals at home in the first half of this competition.

Vitinha with a BEAUTY to put PSG three up after just 30 minutes 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/vgqkI6kI3h.

Recent findings suggest that maybe it was too easy. Maybe City could not continue to be so dominated but it was as if a switch was flicked when the teams returned. The chances came for City. Enzo Fernández should have scored from a close-range header and Haaland did, glancing in an inswinging Ndiaye cross.

Finally the City fans found their voices but then they were silenced. What a calamity for Donnarumma as he got a hand to Akliouche’s shot on the turn, but only palmed the ball up in the air before it bounced into the net.

But City did not stop. Nuno Mendes headed Josko Gvardiol’s flick off the line, Fernández hit a post before Bouaddi set up Haaland and he swept the ball past Safonov.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz.

Sources indicate that there was time for PSG to miss a penalty, with Donnarumma comfortably saving Ferran Torres’s weak effort as City bravely continued to push. They lost, but it did not quite feel like that.

Ruben Amorim will be up against Massimiliano Alvini tomorrow evening, and as the stats show, they are two very different managers.

Sources indicate that as highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, there is one interesting stat to highlight to introduce the game. In terms of shots per game, it will be the second-ranked team and against the 17th-ranked team. That in itself won’t raise any eyebrows, but the fact that Milan are the ones in 17th place will.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that the Rossoneri have mustered a mere 126 shots so far, while Frosinone are quite far ahead at 221. On the flip side, the newly-promoted side have only scored one more goal than Milan (24 vs. 23), which is what makes this game so interesting.

Industry observers note that amorim has made it clear from the start that he wants to dominate each game. That indicates in the possession, as Milan are third in Serie A with an average of 59% so far, and they also rank high in terms of passes per game.

According to recent reports, the shots are where they fall short, even if they average over two goals per game. There are several reasons for this, but most of it can be attributed to Amorim’s recent arrival and the fact that he has experimented rather extensively.

During today’s presser, he even said that they haven’t done anywhere near enough to enter the penalty box more often, which tends to mean more shots.

In the build-up, for example, the Rossoneri move the ball forward at an average speed of 1.30 meters per second, which is the slowest in Serie A. Alvini’s Frosinone, on the other hand, are great at vertical football: the ball moves toward the opponent’s penalty box at 2.51 meters per second, the best rate in the league.

The Ciociari are masters of rapid counterattacks, so much so that on only 40 occasions have they built plays with ten or more passes. Milan, meanwhile, have 203.

Everything starts in the defence phase for Frosinone. Indeed, they always attempt to win the ball back inside the opponent’s half, which is proven by the index that measures the intensity of pressing in the attacking zone (they are first in Serie A).

In a recent development, milan? They are eighth, despite being – along with Como – the team to have scored the most goals (4) from a ball recovered while pressing.

The difference between the two is well explained by the so-called “pressed sequences”, that is, the number of actions in open play in which a team manages to interrupt the opponent’s build-up within three passes or less, before the ball goes beyond the halfway line.

On that front, Frosinone are also first (161), while Milan are only 15th (102). Having remarked all of this, as the pink newspaper concludes, we should expect a spectacular match tomorrow. Both teams will stick to their respective game, which bodes well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As he left Milanello earlier this evening, Gerry Cardinale stopped to share a few words on the game against Frosinone, the January mercato, Markus Krösche and more.

Cardinale arrived in Milan a few days ago and had a summit with the management at Casa Milan yesterday. In other words, he’s not wasting any time, making every second of his trip to the city count.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Today, he was at Milanello to watch the team’s training session and Amorim’s press conference, and tomorrow he will be at the game against Frosinone.

Sources indicate that the owner left the training ground shortly after 4 pm today, but before driving away, he rolled down the window and spoke to the journalists present. In addition to the game, he also spoke about the upcoming mercato and what Milan intend to do.

“I’m ready for tomorrow. We had a great couple of days, including a session at Casa Milan yesterday on the mercato, as well as the rest of our aims for the season going into the summer. I’d say that the mood is really upbeat here, it was a great session today and the team is really coming together.

“I spoke to a bunch of the players, they are all feeling really positive, and they understand as Ruben noted how important tomorrow’s game is. Hopefully, we come out strong, get the win and keep going.”.

“Yeah I’m ready. We are doing a lot of work. It’s complicated and the January transfer window is always tricky. So you have to be prepared, you have to be opportunistic. The one thing I can promise is that we won’t make any decision that we don’t feel great about.

“We will spend money, but we will spend money smart and with a view to being consistent with the project, in close coordination with Ruben and everyone here at Milanello.”.

“With Markus Krösche. I know you guys have been very focused on Markus, but when we’re ready to make an announcement, I will come back to you guys on it.”.

“Look, that name also keeps getting mentioned. This project is more than just one player, but he’s one of the best players, if not the best player, in his position. So tremendous amount of respect from me and we will see what’s possible.”.

“Look, I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. I think he’s just fantastic and I have a tremendous amount of respect for him and his family. We are in discussions and I hope that we will have a good result. But if it were up to me, he would be a franchise player.”.

Industry observers note that clearly, there’s a lot happening right now and Milan are hoping that the addition of Krösche to the management will help them get even better control. It would certainly raise the enthusiasm if they were to have a good mercato and secure a renewal for Adrien Rabiot.

Industry observers note that cardinale: “Ho parlato con i giocatori sono molto concentrati. Endrick e’ uno dei migliori giocatori al mondo, ci proveremo, vediamo se sarà una possibilità di mercato. Rabiot? E’ un giocatore fantastico vogliamo che sia anche per il futuro” https://t.co/bf9mcZulbG.

McInnes believes Cup final incentive will fuel Rangers in vital run of fixtures

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 10:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:13 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 10:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:13 EST, 23 November 2026.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.

A 2-1 triumph over Motherwell on Saturday night stretched Rangers' unbeaten run to 13 matches after Ryan Naderi struck a late winner at Fir Park.

McInnes' side will host a revitalised Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night, before two further home matches against Falkirk and Dundee United over the next week.

They will then face a double-header against Hibs, with a league clash at Easter Road swiftly followed by the cup final.

McInnes insists no player is guaranteed their place in the team - and challenged them to earn their place for the Hampden showpiece as they look to win the first trophy of the season.

'I think the squad looks strong at the minute,' said the Ibrox boss. 'We've got good options and good options from the bench to turn to.

Derek McInnes has led Rangers on a 13-game unbeaten run in all competitions.

'In this little run of fixtures, hopefully everybody will start to play a wee bit more of their part and hopefully more winning performances.

'I don't think I'll mention it [the cup final] too often, but they are not daft, they see that and everybody wants to play in the team.

'Anybody who's in the team needs to keep playing well to stay in the team and anybody who's not in the team needs to train right and take advantage of their minutes.

'We make that point often enough. Sometimes you've got to go away to tough venues like Motherwell and do the hard work and get the reward.

'But there's bigger games, more games like cup finals to take part in, so everybody wants to play in that one.

It has been revealed that 'I'm sure it does us no harm. I think it keeps the fans bubbling along, a chance of silverware, so when it comes along hopefully, as I say, we're in good form.'.

Rangers are on a strong run of form and haven't lost a game since they were dumped out of Europe against Jablonec at the end of August.

The victory over Motherwell maintained their position in second in the table, four points adrift of Celtic with a game in hand.

Up against an Aberdeen side buoyed by their first win under latest boss Mario Frick at the weekend, McInnes wants his players to keep the pedal to the metal.

'I think it's unusual with five games now away from Ibrox, four in the league and the cup game, and now the fixtures kind of run the other way,' said the Rangers boss.

'We've got some good fixtures at home but I think we always look at little blocks in the weeks, and where we're looking to try and get to by a certain period, and get certain points and certain targets.

It has been revealed that 'But first thing's first now with Aberdeen. We've got to make sure we're a strong home team again. Hopefully we can score a few more goals but, ultimately, as long as we win the game, I'll be happy.

'I think there's always a wee concern when you've got so many away on an international break, but obviously now with the January break gone, this is us working right through to March.

'When you look at those little blocks of games, and where the teams are, it's important that we just put our shoulder to the wheel.

Industry observers note that 'Every game is going to bring up different challenges and just because we're at Ibrox, it's an advantage, but it doesn't guarantee anything. We've got to use that advantage properly.

Industry observers note that 'As I say, we've got some fixtures now ahead of the cup final. Hopefully we can get into the cup final in good form and with some strong performances.'.

Venezuelan striker Kevin Kelsy could be in line to start against Aberdeen.

Kevin Kelsy could be in line for a bigger role this week after fatigue caused by his return from international duty limited his involvement in Saturday's win over Motherwell.

The Venezuela striker was only fit enough for a substitute appearance after enduring a gruelling journey back from a friendly in Russia, with Derek McInnes admitting the travel disruption had taken its toll.

'When you go away on international duty, they go to some far-flung places and playing a friendly in Russia is not the best preparation,' said the Rangers boss.

Sources indicate that 'There was a point on Thursday morning when we were really worried about whether he was getting back. To have ten-and-a-half hours in an airport all day Thursday isn't ideal preparation.

'He was gubbed on Friday. He was very tired when he spoke to me and told me he hadn't really slept.

According to recent reports, 'It's been a bit unusual, the preparation. We sent him home early on Friday to get a good sleep and look after himself, but we just made the call we thought was the right thing to do.

'We needed everybody at it on Saturday and we've got a massive week ahead of us where he can play his part, hopefully from the start in one or two of these games.'.

4 managers Lincoln City must target after Chris Cohen, Tom Shaw sacking decision

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that lincoln City slipped to within three points of the Championship relegation zone on Tuesday night as they were thumped 4-0 by Charlton Athletic.
  • Industry observers note that head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw have been relieved of their duties, as confirmed on Wednesday morning.
  • Now, after 19 games in charge, the Imps have opted for change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that lincoln City slipped to within three points of the Championship relegation zone on Tuesday night as they were thumped 4-0 by Charlton Athletic. It made it five consecutive losses for the Imps, and they’ve taken action as a result.

Industry observers note that head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw have been relieved of their duties, as confirmed on Wednesday morning. The duo served as part of Michael Skubala‘s backroom staff in the League One title-winning season, and stepped into the lead role together after the former boss exited for Bristol City.

Now, after 19 games in charge, the Imps have opted for change. Here, we put forward four contenders the club should consider for their vacant position….

In a recent development, given that Lincoln City are likely to be in a Championship relegation battle, they could do with someone who has experience in this league. Among the available bosses, few have the level of second-tier pedigree that Paul Heckingbottom has.

The Yorkshireman was let go by Preston North End after a poor start to the season but he has been there, done that and got the T-shirt in the Championship. Not only has he led successful survival fights, but he took Sheffield United to promotion as well.

Industry observers note that heckingbottom’s pragmatic management can make the most of the squad on offer at Sincil Bank. He can lead them to safety before looking to push up the division in the long term.

A similar but perhaps slightly more ambitious option than Heckingbottom is Steve Cooper. The Welshman is on the market after his spell in charge of Danish side Brondby came to an end in May.

It has been revealed that like Heckingbottom, Cooper has led Championship struggles before and led them up the table. His stint at Nottingham Forest was perhaps the best of his career to date, taking them from the lower reaches of the second tier all the way to the Premier League.

The 46-year-old prioritises a stern defensive structure and organisation out of possession, looking to break on counter-attacks with wide threats. His recent Premier League jobs could make this a tough sell for Lincoln City, but they could tempt him into a key role in their exciting project.

Recent findings suggest that in Juan Carlos Osorio, Lincoln City would be landing a manager whose vast experience and meticulous match preparation could help them stave off relegation from the Championship and build for the next chapter. The 65-year-old has been out of work since March 2026 after a short stint in Brazil with Clube do Remo.

According to recent reports, osorio’s most notable club achievements include a dominant spell in charge of Atlético Nacional from 2012 to 2015, during which he won three league titles and a further three domestic trophies. The Colombian also managed Mexico for three years, winning 33 of 52 games, including a memorable FIFA World Cup group-stage victory over Germany.

Industry observers note that he is no stranger to English football either. Osorio coached at Manchester City early in his career, and he completed his UEFA Pro Licence with the FA, alongside Frank Lampard, Anthony Barry and Michael Carrick. He knows the demands of the English game and the culture of its dressing rooms, so he would need little time to settle.

Industry observers note that naturally, the boss has had highs and lows over the course of a 20-year management career. However, Osorio’s pedigree and attention to detail could make him a hit with the Imps, and his strong connections in South and North American football could open up new avenues for the club’s expanding scouting network.

Last but not least is another left-field option, but a move to appoint 63-year-old Antoine Kombouare would be an eye-catching one, and he’s a good fit too.

Kombouare has been managing since 1999 and over the years, he’s led the likes of PSG, RC Lens and FC Nantes. He was most recently in charge of Paris FC earlier this year, and he helped them take 21 points from 11 Ligue 1 games to stave off relegation before resigning.

Recent findings suggest that he might not have a move to the Championship or Lincoln City in mind, but he is an active and successful manager despite his age. He is a no-nonsense boss known for turning around struggling teams with defensive discipline and mental resilience – two key attributes in a relegation fight.

Kombouare may be an unfeasible option, but perhaps he could be tempted to take on a new challenge in England having spent almost his entire managerial career in France.

Christy Grimshaw was crucial as AC Milan Women finally got back to winning ways, following what was a rather crazy first half against Sassuolo.

Recent findings suggest that after two defeats and a draw, dropping points in a silly fashion against Napoli last weekend, Milan Women needed to bounce back with a win today. Thankfully, that’s exactly what they managed to do, even if it wasn’t the most controlled performance.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that just looking at the scoreline and the timing of the goals is enough to understand the nature of the game. All five goals were scored in the first half and it doesn’t end there either. All five were scored within the first 27 minutes!

The veteran Grimshaw opened the scoring for the Rossonere after nine minutes, but Sassuolo found a way back into the game just two minutes later. The Scottish international decided to restore the lead just four minutes later, i.e. in the 15th minute.

Angelica Soffia then made things more comfortable with a third goal in the 24th minute, or at least so we thought. Just three minutes after that, Sassuolo scored again and thus brought some life into the game, even if Milan looked the better side.

According to recent reports, suzanne Bakker’s side actually dominated possession, had more shots on target and also had a higher xG, so the win definitely feels deserved. And boy was it needed! The situation in the standings is still not great, but at least they are now four points behind the Champions League zone.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.
  • Ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break.
  • Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.

Ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break. However, it won’t be an easy game against Massimiliano Alvani’s Frosinone, who have impressed everyone so far.

Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.

➤ Manager: Massimiliano Alvini ➤ Form (all comps): W-D-W-W-L (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Raimondo – 8 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Kvernadze, Schmid and Ghedjemis – 4 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

Industry observers note that frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are at the moment on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

According to recent reports, it’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

Industry observers note that so, what is behind this rise? As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

Recent findings suggest that it doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly significant-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

In a recent development, moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

Sources indicate that the Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham have slipped down to 12th place in the Championship table following their 1-0 loss away at Portsmouth on Tuesday night.
  • According to recent reports, the Hammers turned to Scott Parker as their head coach earlier this month after their decision to part ways with Nuno Espirito Santo.
  • According to recent reports, brazil, who played for the likes of Ipswich Town, Tottenham Hotspur and QPR during his playing days, has delivered his verdict on the London outfit on talkSPORT: “It’s only four games (for Parker).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham have slipped down to 12th place in the Championship table following their 1-0 loss away at Portsmouth on Tuesday night. WHUFC are now three points off the top eight behind Swansea City.

According to recent reports, the Hammers turned to Scott Parker as their head coach earlier this month after their decision to part ways with Nuno Espirito Santo. However, the ex-Fulham, AFC Bournemouth and Burnley man has struggled to make an impact so far and is yet to win in his first four games at the helm.

According to recent reports, brazil, who played for the likes of Ipswich Town, Tottenham Hotspur and QPR during his playing days, has delivered his verdict on the London outfit on talkSPORT: “It’s only four games (for Parker). I’m sure he can turn that around but defensively they are giving so many easy goals away. They’ve got to stop that.”.

Recent findings suggest that he added: “Listen, I still think they’ll be hovering top six (eight). I was hoping that they’d have a great start. I like West Ham but it hasn’t to be.”.

In a recent development, west Ham are back in action this weekend as they aim to return to winning ways. They take on high flying Stoke City at the London Stadium.

West Ham haven’t kept a clean sheet in their last six matches. As Brazil has alluded to, WHUFC have been leaking too many goals.

Recent findings suggest that the Hammers need to tighten up their defensive department if they are to turn their fortunes around over the coming weeks. They will get the chance to bring in some upcoming faces when the January transfer window opens up for business.

Industry observers note that parker will be eager to put his own stamp on his newly inherited squad this winter. He knows what it takes to get out of the second tier having guided Fulham, AFC Bournemouth and Burnley up in the past.

According to recent reports, he is under pressure already at West Ham though, despite only being four games into his spell. If they lose again against Stoke City on Saturday, the heat will be further intensified.

Industry observers note that west Ham are still the top scorers in the division. WHUFC have scored 38 goals in their 17 fixtures.

The Hammers are always a threat going forward and if they can bolster their backline, there is no reason why they can’t rise back up the league. They managed to keep hold of Jarrod Bowen in the summer and he has found the net on nine occasions this term.

Parker will be disappointed with his start as manager but the players are still getting used to his style. He won’t get patience from the supporters though and needs wins fast.

Bayern Munich could make a move for the AC Milan target and Club Brugge star Nicolo Tresoldi, following Harry Kane’s injury.

Tresoldi has been making waves at Club Brugge this season, scoring an impressive five goals in the Champions League, and Milan are one of several big clubs that have been linked with him. Of course, those links are mainly fueled by the fact that the striker is a big Milan fan.

In a recent development, club Brugge want at least €60m for their star and knowing Bayern Munich’s resources, they would be far more comfortable paying that amount than Milan. In short, Kane’s injury has not only resulted in a headache for the German side, but also for the Rossoneri.

Leeds United, Brentford interested in Leicester City teenager – three European clubs also keen

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, leicester City have seen a handful of new starlets find more regular roles in the first team since their drop to League One.
  • Sources indicate that among them is 18-year-old winger Bismark Owusu, and according to reporter Pete O’Rourke, a string of clubs are interested in prising him away from the King Power Stadium.
  • In a recent development, owusu has been a regular in the Foxes’ U18s side for some time and he has stepped up his involvement in the U21s group this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, leicester City have seen a handful of new starlets find more regular roles in the first team since their drop to League One. Louis Page, Will Alves and Sammy Braybrooke are all mainstays under Russell Martin, and there’s a crop of impressive prospects impressing in the LCFC youth ranks as well.

Sources indicate that among them is 18-year-old winger Bismark Owusu, and according to reporter Pete O’Rourke, a string of clubs are interested in prising him away from the King Power Stadium. Premier League pair Leeds United and Brentford are said to be alongside Italy’s Parma, Dutch side FC Utrecht and FC Copenhagen of Denmark in targeting Owusu.

In a recent development, owusu has been a regular in the Foxes’ U18s side for some time and he has stepped up his involvement in the U21s group this season. He is not yet under a professional contract, but that step could come soon having turned 18 earlier this month.

In a recent development, owusu has been with Leicester City from a young age, progressing through their academy ranks to the U18s, where he plays most of his football now. Despite only just turning 18, he has already made 54 appearances for the Foxes’ side at the age group.

According to recent reports, his progression and strong performances have seen him make his first four appearances for the U21s this season. Owusu has played in the Premier League Cup and International Cup, alongside one substitute outing in Premier League 2 against Nottingham Forest at the start of November.

It has been revealed that the LCFC prospect mainly plays as a winger, but has also been deployed in a central role as an attacking midfielder. He can play on the left or right.

Leicester City have invested huge amounts into their training and academy facilities over the past 10 years. It means they are a great place for young players to hone their craft and develop as players.

Recent findings suggest that although LCFC would obviously have hoped to be playing far above League One level, the drop has paved the way for some of their brighter academy prospects to break into the senior team. The earlier mentioned trio of Page, Alves and Braybrooke have been among this season’s standout performers.

Jayden Joseph has made nine appearances this term, while Bade Aluko and Tommy Neale have also found opportunities.

It highlights players like Owusu that there is a pathway to the first team at the King Power Stadium. They can make the breakthrough they are pursuing with the Foxes, and that can help fend off interest from elsewhere.

#119269. Tech Report: Serie A preview: AC Milan vs. Frosinone – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

Tech Report: Serie A preview: AC Milan vs. Frosinone – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1828 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Milan will return to action on Sunday evening, hoping to pick up where they left off before the international break with a strong performance against Frosinone.
  • If we look at the league, it has been a very decent start to the season for Ruben Amorim and his men.
  • In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Milan will return to action on Sunday evening, hoping to pick up where they left off before the international break with a strong performance against Frosinone.

If we look at the league, it has been a very decent start to the season for Ruben Amorim and his men. However, they are yet to win three games on the trot, so tomorrow’s encounter is a fantastic chance for them to really show their worth.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that it won’t be easy, though. Amorim said during his press conference that it’s hard to identify the movement patterns of Frosinone, who certainly have the ability to make life difficult for the Rossoneri.

Game date: Sunday, November 22 Kick-off time: 18:00 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Luca Pairetto (VAR: Pezzuto).

Some good news arrived on Saturday morning as Strahinja Pavlovic was deemed fit enough to be called up for the game. It’s not certain whether he will start or not, but Amorim at least said that he’s happy to have the Serbian and ‘his fire’ back.

Industry observers note that A few days ago, it was also confirmed that Mike Maignan will be at the manager’s disposal despite the injury scare with France. Of course, it’s not all perfect on the injury front as Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze are still sidelined.

Industry observers note that anyway, moving on to the predicted starting eleven, it was initially thought that Amorim would field the same one as we saw against Genoa. However, he made it very clear during the presser that Musah won’t play as a left-back, so there will indeed be some changes.

According to the latest reports, the American will still start but in midfield instead, allowing Adrien Rabiot to have a slightly more advanced role. It also means that Davide Bartesaghi will come into the eleven, at the moment ahead of Pervis Estupinan in the race.

According to recent reports, alphadjo Cisse has been in red-hot form lately but it seems Amorim wants to manage expectations a little, with the youngster tipped to start on the bench. Christian Pulisic should thus have a role on the flank as opposed to in the centre, although one would imagine everything will be a bit fluid.

According to recent reports, it’s no surprise to see that Goncalo Ramos should start up front, but of course, he will need to get going with the goalscoring sooner rather than later. Francesco Camarda is knocking on the door, as is Cisse who has been tested in that role before.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

According to recent reports, predicted bench: Torriani, P. Terracciano, F. Terracciano, Pavlovic, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Gabbia, Tomori, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze.

Industry observers note that frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

Industry observers note that it’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As pointed out by Gazzetta dello Sport, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

In a recent development, while collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly substantial-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

In a recent development, the Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

This fixture has only been played six times, but even with such a small sample size, it’s clear that Milan are the favourites with four wins and two draws so far. They have won the last three as well, spread across the 2023-24 and 2018-19 seasons.

That said, the most recent encounter was a dramatic one, if you like. Olivier Giroud opened the scoring for Milan away from home but then Frosinone scored twice. Thanks to goals from Matteo Gabbia and Luka Jovic, the Rossoneri were able to turn it back in their favour.

The last time at San Siro, meanwhile, it was a great 3-1 win as Jovic, Pulisic and Tomori found the back of the net. Most of you will remember the American’s goal, as it was Maignan who assisted him with a fantastic pass.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in all six previous meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W4 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

➤ Milan have scored at least three goals in four of their six Serie A matches against Frosinone, producing 15 goals overall, an average of 2.5 per game. Only against Pescara (2.9) have they recorded a higher average, among the opponents they have faced on at least five occasions (2.5 also against Casale and Messina).

Recent findings suggest that ➤ Frosinone have won six games this season, drawing two and losing three. Only three newly promoted teams in the last 40 years have recorded more wins in their first 12 Serie A games of the season: Bari in 1994/95 (seven), Chievo in 2001/02 (seven), and Hellas Verona in 2013/14 (seven).

In a recent development, ➤ Milan have won four of their last five league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in consecutive Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

➤ Although Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their five away games this season (W1 D2), they have won just two of their last 27 away games in Serie A (including previous participations), with 10 draws and 15 defeats.

It has been revealed that ➤ Milan have failed to win four of their last seven Serie A games played after the international break (D2 L2). On the other hand, Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their last five top-flight matches immediately following Italy matches (W2 D1).

It has been revealed that ➤ Frosinone have attempted the most counterattacks from advantageous situations in Serie A this season: 22, almost double the number of any other team. On the other hand, Milan are the only team that haven’t allowed a single counterattack when trailing in the current campaign.

In a recent development, ➤ Only Juventus (79) have attempted more long-range shots than Frosinone (77) this season. On the other hand, Milan are the team that have attempted the fewest shots from outside the area (30) and the one that have conceded the most shots from outside the area in relation to the total conceded, 44%.

Sources indicate that ➤ Adrien Rabiot has earned the most points for his team from direct goal contributions this season, having scored 10 goals and assisted four times. In the most recent matchday, he became the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal in six consecutive league appearances since Kaká in 2004 (who managed seven).

Sources indicate that ➤ Only Matías Soulé (80) has been involved in more sequences ending with a shot than Giacomo Calò (76) in this Serie A. The Frosinone player has scored five goals in the current campaign and only one midfielder has scored more goals in the first 12 matchdays in the top flight for a newly promoted team in the three points for a win era: Hidetoshi Nakata with Perugia in 1998/99 (six).

Since Frosinone like to play on the counterattacks, one player who I think could be crucial for Milan is Musah. As he’s set to start in midfield and not at left-back, the feeling is that his main role will be to prevent the opponents from having too much open space on the counter.

Further up the pitch, I’m excited to see Moreira. He got himself a goal in Belgium’s win over Italy and he has looked a lot better on the right flank ever since the derby performance. He can definitely make the difference with his skill.

As for Frosinone, it’s obvious that Calo is the man whom Milan will want to stop. He likes to dictate the play and if he’s allowed too much time on the ball, identifying his teammates in good positions, then there could be trouble for the Rossoneri.

According to recent reports, it will also be interesting to see if Birigilea can fill the shoes of Raimondo. He bagged a brace against Lecce but in the last two games, he failed to find the back of the net. He will surely be keen to get back on target.

According to recent reports, A lot of people are expecting this to be a high-scoring affair and that’s a very reasonable take, given how both teams play. That said, I think this could be one where Milan actually get their defence in order and don’t concede, even if that might be a somewhat optimistic prediction.

Latest Update: 24-year-old proves he can ease Kim Hellberg’s worries after starring in Middlesbrough’s win over Swansea City

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (538 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that middlesbrough maintained their place at the top of the Championship table on Tuesday night as they defeated managerless Swansea City.
  • It has been revealed that kim Hellberg’s side won 2-1 against the Swans, with Myles Peart-Harris opening the scoring before Joseph Opoku’s equaliser.
  • Industry observers note that as well as scoring the first, midfielder Peart-Harris set up Lankshear’s winner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that middlesbrough maintained their place at the top of the Championship table on Tuesday night as they defeated managerless Swansea City. It marked back-to-back wins for Boro after the return from the international break, following a 2-0 triumph over Bristol City on Saturday.

It has been revealed that kim Hellberg’s side won 2-1 against the Swans, with Myles Peart-Harris opening the scoring before Joseph Opoku’s equaliser. Star striker Will Lankshear was back amongst the goals to net the second and secure the three points.

Industry observers note that as well as scoring the first, midfielder Peart-Harris set up Lankshear’s winner. The 24-year-old started for Middlesbrough and his performance will have come as reassurance for Hellberg given his recent midfield blows.

Earlier this week, Hellberg expressed a desire to reinforce his midfield in the January transfer window. Middlesbrough have lost Rokas Pukstas and Connor Barron to injury, meaning that the only natural players in a deeper role are usual starters Aidan Morris and Sebastian Berhalter.

According to recent reports, peart-Harris, like Riley McGree, can and has played in a deeper role, but is more effective further forward. However, the former Oxford United and Brentford man indicated his quality alongside Morris against Swansea City.

Sources indicate that hellberg’s tactics mean Peart-Harris was able to progress into advanced areas. He was lurking in the 18-yard box before being found by Neto Borges’ pull-back and cleverly side-footing into the bottom corner.

Industry observers note that for Lankshear’s goal, Peart-Harris just about beat the Swans’ offside trap and ran through before squaring it for the striker to convert. Both goals revealed the freedom he had to advance, despite being down as one of Hellberg’s deeper midfield players on paper.

He was able to progress the ball with strong running and forward-thinking passing when in deeper areas. Peart-Harris spent much of the game operating on the right-hand side of the middle third of the pitch, and he was effective for Boro.

Recent findings suggest that hellberg’s lack of depth in midfield is a justified concern, especially coming into the hectic festive schedule. However, Peart-Harris’ performance against Swansea City showed he is ready to step in for Middlesbrough when Morris and Berhalter need a rest.

It was his best display in a Boro shirt to date, and if he can maintain a high level, he’ll be a valuable squad player to have throughout a demanding 2026/27 promotion push.

The performance doesn’t decrease the need for another midfielder, but it shows that Hellberg should be able to deal with the shortage until the opportunity to sign a reinforcement arises.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim is expected to make one change to the starting eleven for Milan-Frosinone, according to the latest reports.

In a recent development, as the international break is over, Milan have used the last couple of days to prepare for Sunday’s clash against Frosinone. It’s a chance for the Rossoneri to make it three consecutive wins for the first time in the league this season, but as highlighted by Amorim, it’s a tough one.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The good news is that Mike Maignan is available despite the injury scare mid-week, while Strahinja Pavlovic has also been included in the squad. Amorim actually stated that the Serbian wants to play, but it would be silly to rush him back.

Recent findings suggest that according to MilanNews, it will be a 4-3-3 formation with Davide Bartesaghi returning as the starting left-back. Yunus Musah will move into the midfield, while Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic will occupy the flanks in attack.

Since Pavlovic seemingly isn’t ready to start, Sankhoun Diawara will keep his spot alongside Koni De Winter in the heart of the defence. The biggest surprise is, of course, that Alphadjo Cisse is tipped to start on the bench. He has been in great form lately, so some might question that decision.

Sky Italia is suggesting that it could be more of a 4-4-1-1, with Rabiot having a free role to move as he pleases.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Industry observers note that predicted bench: Torriani, P. Terracciano, F. Terracciano, Pavlovic, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Pierre Sage’s Lyon return ends in disappointment for Crystal Palace

📅 15 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5096 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.
  • Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.
  • Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” noted Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

“I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

Recent findings suggest that “When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”.

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

Sources indicate that sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

He told Uefa: “It’s a very disappointing return because we lost. I can’t take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn’t there.

“The scoreline may have been close, but there was a substantial difference in the way the two teams played.

“We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

“I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half.”.

The veteran captain said: “It has been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we’re very happy with the performance.”.

When asked about Evanilson’s header, which Smith supplied the assist for, he replied: “It wasn’t my best cross but I put it in an area, what a finish from him and I think we deserved that little bit of luck.

“From there on we went on to win the game but in the second half we got a little bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great and we look forward to Sunday now.

“It’s a great header, he deserved it because he has worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.”.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

Industry observers note that palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.
