General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

The last 7 permanent Rochdale AFC managers ranked from worst to best

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1441 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It is fair to say it has been a difficult start to life back in League Two for Rochdale.
  • Despite missing out on the National League title last season after a heartbreaking final day draw with York City, Rochdale secured promotion back to the EFL following a three-year absence after a dramatic play-off final victory over Boreham Wood.
  • However, just a few weeks after Dale's Wembley success, head coach Jimmy McNulty departed the club to take over at League One side Stockport County, with Ian Watson making the move from National League North side South Shields to replace him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is fair to say it has been a difficult start to life back in League Two for Rochdale.

Despite missing out on the National League title last season after a heartbreaking final day draw with York City, Rochdale secured promotion back to the EFL following a three-year absence after a dramatic play-off final victory over Boreham Wood.

However, just a few weeks after Dale's Wembley success, head coach Jimmy McNulty departed the club to take over at League One side Stockport County, with Ian Watson making the move from National League North side South Shields to replace him.

Unfortunately for Watson, his tenure at the Crown Oil Arena proved to be short-lived, with Rochdale making the decision to part company with the 40-year-old on Sunday after a poor run of form left them just above the League Two relegation zone.

As Dale begin their search for Watson's replacement, we looked back and ranked the club's last seven permanent managers from worst to best.

After his reign came to an end, it is unlikely that many Rochdale fans will hold positive memories of Watson's time at the club.

Watson's South Shields side narrowly missed out on the National League North title to AFC Fylde last season before losing to Kidderminster Harriers in the play-off final, so he looked to be an exciting appointment for the Dale this summer after his impressive work in non-league.

However, the jump up two divisions proved to be too much for Watson, who won just six of his 22 games in charge, drawing three and losing 13, and, as well as the poor results, the lack of a clear style of play and his decision to sideline some of last season's promotion-winning team in favour of his own signings attracted criticism from the fanbase.

It was always going to be tough for anyone to fill McNulty's shoes, particularly for a manager with no previous EFL experience, but Watson's spell at the Crown Oil Arena is one that all parties will be keen to forget.

When Rochdale poached John Coleman from Accrington Stanley in January 2012, it was viewed as something of a coup for the club.

Coleman had established a reputation as one of the best lower league managers during his 13-year stint at Accrington, taking the reformed club into the EFL for the first time in 2006 before building a consistently competitive League Two side.

Having earned his stripes in the fourth tier, the move to Rochdale offered Coleman the chance to show what he could do at League One level, but after taking over with the club sitting towards the bottom of the table, he was unable to prevent their relegation.

Given his strong League Two record, Dale stuck with Coleman following relegation, but the expected promotion push failed to materialise, and the 63-year-old was sacked midway through the campaign in January 2013 after winning just 15 of his 52 games in charge, drawing 12 and losing 25.

After a nightmare start to the 2022-23 season, Rochdale turned to League Two survival expert Jim Bentley.

Dale had picked up just one point from their first six league games and were bottom of the table when Bentley arrived, but the 50-year-old had navigated plenty of fourth tier relegation battles during his eight-and-a-half year spell at Morecambe, so he looked to have the credentials to keep the club in the division.

Bentley inspired an initial upturn in form after taking over at the Crown Oil Arena to lift Rochdale out of the bottom two, but it was not long until their fortunes declined again, resulting in his dismissal in March 2023 with the club sitting 10 points from safety with eight games remaining.

While Bentley won just seven of his 36 games in charge, drawing seven and losing 22, it would be unfair to put too much blame on him for Dale's eventual relegation to the National League given the on and off-field concerns he experienced during his tenure.

After their relegation from League One, Rochdale handed Robbie Stockdale his first senior managerial role in the summer of 2021.

Stockdale had spells as a coach with the likes of Grimsby Town, Sunderland, Hibernian and West Bromwich Albion prior to taking over at the Crown Oil Arena, and Dale would have hoped he could translate his coaching potential into success in the dugout.

Rochdale supporters may have been hoping Stockdale could lead them to promotion from League Two at the first attempt, but the club's limited budget meant that was always going to be unlikely, and the 46-year-old oversaw an underwhelming 18th-placed finish in his debut season.

After Dale lost their opening four games of the 2022-23 season, Stockdale was sacked after just over a year in charge, departing having won 16, drawn 18 and lost 25 of his 59 games at the helm.

Brian Barry-Murphy scored one goal and provided 11 assists in 77 appearances for Rochdale after joining from near neighbours Bury in July 2010, but his on-field exploits would only be the start of a lengthy association with the club.

In addition to his playing duties, Barry-Murphy took up a coaching role at the Crown Oil Arena in 2013, and he stepped in as caretaker manager in March 2019 following the departure of Keith Hill before being handed the permanent job the folllowing month.

Barry-Murphy successfully kept Dale in League One in the 2018-19 and 2019-20 seasons, but he was unable to repeat the trick for a third time in the 2020-21 campaign as his side were relegated, but they certainly did not go down without a fight.

In their relegation season, Rochdale were known as one of the great entertainers in the third tier, and they scored an impressive total of 61 goals throughout the campaign, but defensive frailities ultimately cost Barry-Murphy's men as they also conceded 78 goals.

Barry-Murphy won 35 of his 109 games in charge of Dale prior to his exit in the summer of 2021, drawing 25 and losing 49, but while relegation remains a black mark on the Irishman's CV, supporters of his former club may not be surprised by the subsequent success he has achieved with Cardiff City.

After making 237 appearances during an eight-year spell at the Crown Oil Arena, Jimmy McNulty is another former Rochdale player who went on to manage the club.

McNulty had two caretaker stints in charge of Dale in the 2022-23 season following the dismissals of Stockdale and Bentley, and while he was unable to prevent the club from dropping out of the EFL for the first time in their history, the improved end-of-season form under his guidance was enough to earn him the permanent job.

Rochdale finished 11th and fourth in the National League respectively during McNulty's first two seasons in charge before accumulating a remarkable 106-point haul last season, but although that was not enough to beat York to the title, they sealed a deserved promotion back to League Two with a penalty shootout victory over Boreham Wood at Wembley.

McNulty departed in June to take over at another of his former clubs in Stockport, but the 41-year-old delivered some unforgettable moments during his tenure, which saw him win 80, draw 35 and lose 43 of his 158 games in charge.

Who do you think is the best of Rochdale's recent permanent managers? Tell us in the comments below!

While McNulty produced one of the most memorable campaigns in Rochdale history last season, many supporters will agree that Keith Hill will go down as the club's best manager in recent times.

Hill first took caretaker charge of Dale in December 2006 before being given the permanent job the following month, and he led the club to promotion to League One in the 2009-10 season before making the move to Championship side Barnsley in June 2011.

The 57-year-old returned to the Crown Oil Arena for a second spell in January 2013, and he guided Rochdale to promotion from League Two once again in the 2013-14 campaign before overseeing their record finish of eighth in League One the following season.

There were plenty of other notable highlights during Hill's second stint, including a 2-2 draw at home to Premier League giants Tottenham Hotspur in the FA Cup fifth round in the 2017-18 season which earned a replay at Wembley, as well as a miraculous escape from relegation in the same campaign.

Across his two spells as Rochdale manager, Hill won 242, drew 131 and lost 197 of his 570 games in charge, and his legacy at the club will be secure for a long time to come.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal against Leny Yoro’s red card during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, with captain Bruno Fernandes among those questioning the decision.

Industry observers note that the French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak outside the penalty area. Referee Sam Barrott ruled that Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

Industry observers note that according to Sky Sports, United intend to challenge the decision, with Isak’s chances of regaining possession central to the dispute. Mauricio Pochettino questioned whether Isak would have reached the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, a view shared by midfielder Kobbie Mainoo.

Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”.

It has been revealed that “To make a mistake like this can change a game,” he mentioned, as reported by the Press Association. The Portuguese midfielder nevertheless accepted that United were responsible for conceding from the subsequent free-kick.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher offered a different assessment on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch programme, supporting Barrott’s decision while acknowledging the uncertainty over whether Isak would have reached the ball before Lammens.

“I think most people would have expected a red card,” Gallagher stated.

An attacker’s likelihood of retaining or regaining possession is among the factors referees must consider when assessing whether a foul has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

According to recent reports, united host Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday in Pochettino’s first home match in charge. Unless the appeal succeeds, Yoro will serve a one-match suspension against the Bees. United sit 19th in the Premier League, having won just one of their opening 11 matches. Yoro remains eligible for Wednesday’s Champions League fixture against Sporting, before attention turns to a crucial domestic fixture for Pochettino’s side.

AC Milan resume their Serie A campaign after the final international break on 2026 by welcoming Frosinone to San Siro.

Industry observers note that ruben Amorim’s side are in need of a win to climb back into the top four after Como’s result on Saturday, while Roma and Lazio also picked up victories. They face a Frosinone team who will be full of confidence after an excellent start to their campaign, following promotion in 2025-26.

The latest team news suggests that Amorim will go with a 4-4-1-1 formation, though in his pre-match press conference he did not give too much away about his selection choices, especially in view of Thursday’s trip to Greece.

Recent findings suggest that at the risk of sounding like a broken record, something simply has to click for Goncalo Ramos, and preferably soon. He has gone one month without a goal and his struggles to even generate shots followed him to Portugal on international duty. However, Frosinone are a side that score goals but also let them in too, so there should be spaces to exploit.

Recent findings suggest that it will be an intriguing battle between the No.9 and Gabriele Calvani, while it could even be an audition of sorts for the centre-back. Milan have been linked with the Genoa loanee, who has made an impressive start to the campaign, so it will be an up-close look as he tries to pile the misery on Ramos.

According to recent reports, with top scorer Antonio Raimondo out injured, Giorgi Kvernadze will be the main goal threat for the away side. The Georgian’s seven goal contributions are only bettered by the Italian striker, and he has started all 11 games under Alvini so far in Serie A.

It seems that Mario Gila will be tasked with stopping Kvernadze. The Spaniard spent the break at Milanello after not being called up by Spain again, and he should slot in as the right-sided defender again next to Koni De Winter.

Moving into midfield, there will be a fascinating contest between Adrien Rabiot and Giacomo Calo. It starts with a very obvious point of comparison: both are known for their goal scoring prowess, with the Frenchman already on five for the season and the Italian having racked up the same number.

The pair are likely to face each other head-to-head too. Whereas Rabiot has usually played deeper like Calo, it seems that the head coach is thinking of moving him further forward to play behind Ramos, so he will see a lot of Calo and also Patrizio Masini.

Alvini is expected to give the nod to Aleksa Terzic at left-back, which is notable because the Serbian has only started one game so far in 2026-27, with his other four appearances all coming off the bench. He does like to get forward in transition though, and has a goal to his name.

Sources indicate that primarily, Terzic will be tasked with trying to limit Diego Moreira’s impact on the game. The Belgian – who scored for his national team for the first time in their rout of Italy – is expected to start on the right for the Rossoneri, and his seven goal contributions in seven games tell their own story.

In a recent development, finally, we return to the middle of the park where Luka Modric and Romano Schmid will headline as series of interesting duels. Modric’s importance to Milan in all phases of the game have been written about at length, but particularly the build-up phase in games where his team are expected to dominate the ball.

The Croatian is the metronome for the Rossoneri just as the summer signing Schmid is for the Canarini. The Austrian has been playing mostly as an attacking midfielder, with two goals and four assists to his name, and starts in all 11 rounds thus far.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino reportedly wants to sign a striker in the January transfer window, with Benjamin Sesko not expected to return from injury until the fresh year at the earliest.

According to recent reports, the Argentine’s first match in charge ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, leaving United 19th in the Premier League with just one victory from their opening 11 matches. While defensive shortcomings attracted much of the criticism following the defeat at Anfield, strengthening United’s attack appears to be a priority for the new head coach.

Industry observers note that according to The Times, United’s hierarchy and Pochettino agree that the squad requires strengthening in January, despite the club’s preference for conducting major transfer business during the summer. Sesko’s prolonged absence has limited United’s attacking options, while Joshua Zirkzee has scored just 11 goals in 86 appearances since joining from Bologna’s Serie A rivals Fiorentina in 2024.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been identified as a potential target. The United States international worked under Pochettino at international level and has expressed a desire to leave the French club.

In a recent development, writing in The Independent, Miguel Delaney suggests United could have scope to spend £150m in January, although such expenditure would affect the club’s longer-term recruitment looks. That figure does not represent a confirmed transfer budget, and United have yet to announce any agreement to sign a new striker.

In a recent development, pochettino’s immediate challenge is finding a solution with his existing squad. United face Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday before returning to domestic action against Brentford.

With more than a month before the transfer window opens, the Argentine has little choice but to find a way of improving United’s attacking output with the players already at his disposal.

  • The Owls' winning start to League One life under the former Stockport County boss was halted by a goalless draw against last season's play-off semi-finalists, Stevenage, at the SPORTA Arena on Tuesday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dave Challinor has issued a clear transfer message after just three games as Sheffield Wednesday's new head coach, with the January window now just over one month away from opening.

The Owls' winning start to League One life under the former Stockport County boss was halted by a goalless draw against last season's play-off semi-finalists, Stevenage, at the SPORTA Arena on Tuesday.

Wednesday are at the moment fourth in the table, having taken 27 points from their first 16 encounters, just five less than Challinor's former employers who top the standings.

The upcoming window is just the second of the Arise Capital era at Hillsborough, and the first in which the 51-year-old will be reunited with former Stockport chief, Simon Wilson, who is now the Steel City side's sporting director.

However, it feels rather apparent that Challinor has already dropped a transfer hint to the hierarchy.

Wednesday's squad have certainly shared their 27 goals so far this season around, with Jamal Lowe currently topping the individual charts with seven.

When all fit and available, Challinor has plenty of attacking options at his disposal, including Ali Al-Hamadi, Harry Gray, Mason Burstow, Davis Keillor-Dunn and Louie Barry.

Yet, whilst Keillor-Dunn has impressed in recent weeks with his own four-goal haul, the Owls boss has admitted that the club lacks a natural centre-forward ahead of the January window.

It has been revealed that “We definitely are,” he stated. “With Ali being out, he's (Keillor-Dunn) probably the closest. Harry, I think, will develop into a nine. But as an 18-year-old playing in League One, the physical part of that tour is going to be tough for him.

Recent findings suggest that “They are hard to come by because a number nine, you're looking for the complete centre-forward, aren't you? Somebody that can hold the ball up when you go up to them, is an aerial threat, still wants to be able to run behind, gets themselves in the box when a cross is coming in," he added.

"Difficult to find if I was looking for them. I hope that we get the answers from what we've already got in the building, but we've got time to time to judge that.”.

Despite the attraction Wednesday have in League One in terms of stature, realising such transfer wishes could be difficult for the South Yorkshire side to realise.

Keillor-Dunn's short-term loan from Wrexham is a prime example, as, irrespective of the 28-year-old's quality in the division, only an agreement until January could be struck due to budgeting restraints, with the club still working under a strict business plan from the EFL having exited administration in the summer.

An unwanted return to the Racecourse Ground from the Owls' perspective could free up much-needed funds, but with the January window notoriously hard for doing business in, there are no guarantees that Challinor can solve such a conundrum with players from elsewhere.

There is a consensus amongst Wednesdayites that more quality is needed in attack, despite the blend of experience and energy which is at Challinor's disposal.

Five goals within his first two league encounters against Plymouth Argyle and Barnsley demonstrates exactly what this squad is capable of, but despite having six attempts on target against Stevenage, none of Keillor-Dunn, Barry, the returning Al-Hamadi and Jamal Lowe could find target.

Owls fans, is a latest striker the main priority for Dave Challinor in January? Comment below!

Burstow is set to return from a groin problem in the coming weeks, meaning that, in the short-term, at least, Wednesday are not short of options, and it would certainly be beneficial for those names to fire goals in on a regular given the lack of potential wriggle room in the transfer market.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Raul Jimenez could be seen joining in the celebrations after Adam Armstrong’s excellent volley for Wolves sealed an emphatic 3-0 win over Derby County.

Cesar Peixoto’s side are starting to hit their stride, as the victory against the Rams made it eight unbeaten for Wolves ahead of a weekend trip to struggling Lincoln City.

However, perhaps the most encouraging aspect of the three points against Derby was the performance, as Wolves battered the visitors, recording 39 shots on goal.

Despite the overall dominance, John Eustace’s men actually started brightly at Molineux, as they put the hosts under pressure and had a few chances to take the lead.

But, Wolves were always a threat, and they took the lead when Armstrong slotted home after good work from Mane.

Wanderers missed chance after chance in the second half, but the talented teenager put the game to bed as he got his first goal of the campaign with a side-footed finish.

Armstrong then made it three, which reflected Wolves’ superiority, with a great volley that wowed the home fans - and it also got Jimenez on his feet.

That’s after footage was shared on social media of the Mexican applauding his teammate as he looked very impressed with Armstrong’s effort.

It’s great for Wolves fans to see Jimenez in the stands like a fan even though he is out injured, as it indicates what the club means to him.

Of course, his legendary status at Molineux is already secured, but the fact he is out watching the team on a cold night in November means a lot to the supporters, and he has also been present at various club events in recent weeks.

Jimenez and his family have bought into what Wolves and the city are all about, and even though he hasn’t played for months, Peixoto was keen to point out the influence that the striker has had on the dressing room even in his absence.

And, seeing his reaction to Armstrong’s goal, it is an example of a team with a good spirit and togetherness, which will be crucial if Wolves are going to win promotion.

Following on from that, Wolves will feel they are starting to click into gear as they chase an immediate return to the Premier League, especially when you consider they will have Jimenez back in January.

Even though they’ve been very good in terms of their points return all season, the win over Derby felt like a statement one in the sense that they really looked devastating going forward for the first time in a while.

Armstrong has been key to that with his movement, intelligence and excellent finishing, but the prospect of adding Jimenez to this team is one that should worry Wolves’ promotion rivals.

Will Wolves win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

The 35-year-old will give Wolves a physical profile up front, which means they have another way of playing, and if Jimenez and Armstrong can combine later in the campaign, Peixoto’s side could stack up a few more significant wins over the coming months.

Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino could have less than £50million to spend in January, leaving the Argentine with limited room to spend during the winter transfer window.

According to reports from the Daily Mail, United are working within financial restrictions and are unlikely to sanction any major spending in January. The club are also mindful of the Premier League’s financial regulations, which could make it difficult to fund major names.

However, the budget means Pochettino may have to choose his priorities carefully rather than address every problem in one window.

Industry observers note that united recorded revenue of £677.6million despite not playing European football last season. However, the Premier League’s Squad Cost Ratio rules restrict spending on player and head coach wages, transfer repayments and agent fees to 85 per cent of football revenue, plus net profit from player sales.

January could become a window of careful decisions for United and Pochettino but looking at their current position and form, they need far more than just 50 million. In this budget, Pochettino needs to be careful who he brings in to improve their standings.

Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne insisted that any potential punishment for breaching financial rules will not change what Pep Guardiola’s team achieved and their memories of success.

The Belgian was a key pillar during the spell of unprecedented domestic dominance and has a statue commissioned outside the Etihad Stadium.

De Bruyne is back in town with Napoli for Tuesday’s Champions League tie, reiterating his ‘love’ for City and its owners, while revealing recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

The 35-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal and were sanctioned after being found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them.

De Bruyne’s trophy haul – six Premier League titles, one Champions League, two FA Cups and five Carabao Cups – were largely secured outside of the nine-year period in which City were scrutinised, up to 2018.

It has been revealed that ‘I’m proud of what I've done as a football player,’ De Bruyne said. ‘Honestly, this is my club, I love the owners. I've talked about a lot of stuff outside football (with them), I've even spoken to Khaldoon about how to buy a club and everything.

The 36-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal.

In a recent development, ‘It (stripping of titles) still doesn't change (anything), my football has not changed. I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played.

‘But everybody has his own opinion and other people may be disgraced a bit. I can't change anything about that.’.

De Bruyne’s final two seasons at City were plagued by injury before he joined Napoli on a free transfer in 2025 and his first return in last year’s Champions League lasted just 26 minutes as he hobbled off.

Classed as the greatest player in the club’s modern history, De Bruyne was typically forthright on the uncertainty surrounding his former employers after the guilty verdicts read by a three-person independent commission.

Recent findings suggest that ‘My feelings have never been different,’ he added. ‘Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group.

In a recent development, ‘Of course, it's a lot of things that have been going on. I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change. Even now, the people who treated me and my family for 10 years is the most important thing.’.

De Bruyne left City under duress, vehemently disagreeing with the club’s decision not to offer him a new contract following a spate of injuries before choosing Napoli – and his long-term future in Serie A is now appearing in doubt.

Sources indicate that all eyes in Italy were on the midfielder’s public response to an interview published with his wife, Michele, in which she was reported to have criticised life in Naples and yearned for a move away. Those comments were taken out of context, according to a visibly frustrated De Bruyne, with PSV Eindhoven looking at securing a transfer in January.

De Bruyne left City under duress but revealed recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

But City supporters will have been more interested in how far De Bruyne went in backing their club ahead of next month’s appeal hearing.

‘In life there are rules, but everybody plays to the limit, I would say,’ he claimed, seemingly referring to how financial rules are interpreted by the Premier League’s elite clubs.

‘I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams.

‘So for me that's the thing that I value most. The most important thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things, and I've given my all.’.

De Bruyne smirked as he discussed how he knew exactly how City would attack Napoli given his knowledge of the club and manager Enzo Maresca, who was Guardiola’s assistant during the 2023 Treble campaign.

Maresca is facing criticism after three defeats and a draw in their last four league games. The Italian called for calm over recent performances and believes that the transition from Guardiola was always going to represent a bumpy road.

‘It's like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method,’ Maresca stated.

It has been revealed that ‘It's not easy to all of a sudden change. For me personally, it's all normal, and hopefully as soon as possible we can find the right balance in all the lines - defensive, midfield - and we can be consistent, which for me is the difference between us and other clubs.’.

5 Chris Cohen & Tom Shaw replacements Lincoln City must eye ASAP

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1551 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lincoln City have confirmed the sacking of dual head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw following a disastrous run of form, with the pair having only succeeded Michael Skubala over the summer.
  • The Imps elected to promote internally upon Skubala's bombshell departure to Championship rivals Bristol City after guiding the side to the second-tier for the first time since 1961 by romping to the League One title, which left their key decision-makers to opt against hiring an external candidate.
  • Instead, Lincoln placed faith in the abilities of Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw as the duo played vital roles in the club's success under Skubala.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lincoln City have confirmed the sacking of dual head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw following a disastrous run of form, with the pair having only succeeded Michael Skubala over the summer.

The Imps elected to promote internally upon Skubala's bombshell departure to Championship rivals Bristol City after guiding the side to the second-tier for the first time since 1961 by romping to the League One title, which left their key decision-makers to opt against hiring an external candidate.

Instead, Lincoln placed faith in the abilities of Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw as the duo played vital roles in the club's success under Skubala.

They would, however, ultimately fall short of continuing the Imps' upwards direction of travel, and have been relieved of their duties after a losing streak was extended to five matches by falling to a chastening 4-0 defeat at the hands of Charlton Athletic on Tuesday evening.

Lincoln have won just four of their opening 17 matches in the Championship and are positioned merely three points above 22nd-placed Preston North End, who themselves are on the rise following a three-match unbeaten streak, and with eight losses from the last ten, the second-tier newcomers simply had to make a change in order to retain prospects of achieving survival.

With Lincoln having already confirmed the initiation of a recruitment process to seek out a replacement, Football League World has decided to take a close look at FIVE candidates that the strugglers should be setting their sights on in the coming days.

Heading proceedings underway is Matt Bloomfield, who wouldn't represent the most pulse-racing or wildcard appointment in the world but could just be worth a punt from the Imps' key decision-makers.

His managerial career has been something of a rollercoaster already, with the former midfielder initially shining in charge of Wycombe Wanderers and mounting a shock title race alongside Birmingham City before leaving for Luton Town, suffering relegation from the Championship and then being dismissed out of Kenilworth Road months later.

According to recent reports, clearly, then, it was an ill-fated decision to leave Wycombe in the first place, and it's one which Bloomfield is perhaps yet to recover from. He wasn't able to keep Oxford United afloat after succeeding Gary Rowett either, and while the appointment of Aaron Ramsey has since proven an extremely-shrewd one, Bloomfield's sacking still felt harsh back in the summer.

Sources indicate that bloomfield's best work, of course, came at Wycombe, where relatively-modest expectations and financial resources during much of his tenure clearly worked in his favour. It would be rather similar with Lincoln, although the Imps' situation could also be comparable to Oxford's and the fact that he failed to keep the Yellows alive in the second-tier is an obvious caveat.

Still, Bloomfield is just 43 and has time on his side to turn his stock around - and Lincoln could do much worse than providing him that opportunity.

A much more high-risk, high-reward appointment, meanwhile, could come in the form of Calum McFarlane, who was tenuously linked with the top job at Sincil Bank over the summer.

Whether there was anything at all in those links is yesterday's news. Now, with Lincoln on the search for a new boss once again, McFarlane is somebody who should be coming under serious consideration, and he would fit the club's head-coach model much more seamlessly than other candidates.

The highly-rated Chelsea coach is currently working as Xabi Alonso's assistant after taking interim charge at Stamford Bridge during the back-end of the previous season following Liam Rosenior's departure, and has built up an encouraging reputation in West London.

Calm under pressure, progressive in his methods and experienced in coaching young talent from his days leading Chelsea's academy sides, McFarlane's stock is on the rise and Lincoln should be testing the waters to see whether a first senior, full-time gig could tempt the 41-year-old away from the Premier League giants.

These hires typically go one of two ways, but the potential upside is clear to see.

Lincoln have rarely been ones to shy away from left-field hires in the dugout, having done so with both Cohen and Shaw and the aforementioned Skubala, yet they shouldn't dismiss the possibility of taking that one step further with a more continental approach to mirror an overarching part of their player recruitment strategy.

Wilfried Nancy has never coached in England, and the Frenchman's stock has taken a notable hit following his disastrous short-lived reign at Celtic nearly a year ago. He won just two of his eight games in charge of the Hoops and departed under a cloud with the worst record of any boss on either side of the Old Firm divide, yet that alone should not completely overlook a fantastic of body of work in the MLS before jetting off across the Atlantic.

Nancy initially started off in senior coaching by succeeding Thierry Henry at CF Montreal, and finished his time with the Canada-based outfit with the second-best record in the Eastern Conference back in 2022. He went one better after joining Columbus Crew, where he would win the 2023 MLS Cup before winning the MLS Coach of the Year while earning wide plaudits for an attractive, possession-heavy brand of football.

Known for playing a 3-4-2-1 shape with interchanging roles and an emphasis on dominating the ball with attacking overloads and a high tempo both in and out of possession, Nancy follows the ilk of many modern-day head coaches by unequivocally sticking to his principles.

Many Celtic fans felt as though that was his downfall at Parkhead, whereas there would have to be questions as to whether he'd even be able to get Lincoln players to carry out such tactical and technical demands.

Nonetheless, Nancy is one of the more gifted and high-ceiling coaches that Lincoln could hire - even if it would be a wildcard call of the high-risk, high-reward genre.

Bo Henriksen's style, meanwhile, would be much more suitable for what remains a primarily pragmatic, dynamic and aggressive Imps side, yet his appointment undoubtedly represents a more ambitious call.

The Danish coach, who spent three surprising years in English football with Kidderminster Harriers and Bristol Rovers during a largely-unremarkable playing career, has earned an impressive reputation on the continent, and it's one that could just put him out of Lincoln's reach.

That's not to say that Lincoln shouldn't be asking the question, though, as Henriksen would be a superb appointment. He started off with FC Midtjylland before taking Zurich from the foot of the league table after ten games to a mid-table finish, and then earned a move to Mainz 05 as a result of his work in Switzerland.

In a recent development, mainz enjoyed a rich run of form under Henriksen, who led them from relegation trouble to 13th place with a nine-match unbeaten streak at the end of the 2023/24 term. They went even better the following season and left fans across Germany shocked by reaching third place in late March, before losing their footing and settling for a UEFA Europa Conference League spot instead.

Sources indicate that it was a strong season regardless, yet Henriksen would fall short of matching those standards and received his marching orders in December of last year following one win from his opening 12 games. Interestingly, he has been out of work ever since and Lincoln should be pulling out all the stops to seal his return to management.

Unlike Nancy, for example, Henriksen is not in the modern-day possession-heavy coaching mold and instead focuses on a high-energy approach involving intense pressing out of possession and quick transitions. He's known as something of a culture-builder, too, often instilling belief, fight and energy into struggling squads low on confidence, with those attributes earmarking him as exactly what Lincoln need right now.

Of all the listed candidates, he could just be the best pick of the lot.

The fifth and final boss who should be coming under Lincoln's consideration is Jimmy Thelin, who has been unattached since his sacking from Aberdeen in January of this year.

Thelin enjoyed success leading Elfsborg in his native Sweden between 2018 and 2024, and 2023 was a particularly notable year as he won the Allsvenskan Coach of the Year after guiding his side to an impressive third-placed finish.

According to recent reports, that form put him on the radar of Aberdeen, who made a remarkable start under his stewardship in 2024/25 by winning 10 of his opening 11 games in charge. They did, however, take only five wins from the remaining 27 - yet still managed to win their first trophy in eleven years by beating Celtic in the Scottish Cup final.

In a recent development, lincoln City fans, what do you make of FLW's selections? Who would be your number-one choice? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

Thelin never managed to sustain his early-season form at Aberdeen and was later sacked at the start of the year, which makes him a realistic yet somewhat-ambitious potential candidate for Lincoln to target.

The 48-year-old Swede, who was linked with the Sheffield Wednesday job just last month, is known to be keen on managing in England and that would only help the Imps' chances if they decided to court his services.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

It has been revealed that “The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino stated.

Industry observers note that “Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”.

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

“But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

Industry observers note that the FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Premier League and England international defender, Conor Coady, has reportedly emerged as a leading contender to replace Ian Evatt at League One strugglers, Blackpool.

That is according to an update from Pete O'Rourke via X, with the Tangerines beginning third-tier life without their former defender with one point from a possible six.

A 2-1 loss to Lancashire rivals, Wigan Athletic, at Bloomfield Road on Saturday lunchtime was followed up by an encouraging draw against Russell Martin's in-form Leicester City on Tuesday night, with Niall Ennis equalising Will Alves' opener.

Blackpool are currently 20th in League One having taken just 13 points from 15 matches, and whilst the club still have a game in hand to play over many divisional rivals, only a two-goal swing separates them and Doncaster Rovers, who occupy the final relegation place.

Blackpool have endured mixed fortunes since their relegation from the Championship three-and-a-half years ago, with whoever replaces Evatt being the fifth head coach at Bloomfield Road since then.

Evatt was able to guide the Seasiders to a 13th-placed finish last season, ending the campaign with four wins on the bounce, but departed the club last week on his 45th birthday, and attention has now turned as to who will be his successor in the long run.

Steve Thompson led the fixtures against Wigan and Leicester, but as per O'Rourke, it has been claimed that Coady, 33, has emerged as a 'top contender' for the role, just weeks after confirming his retirement from playing.

The centre-back amassed over 300 combined appearances at Premier League and Championship level, and is best known for his spells at Liverpool, Wolves, Everton and Wrexham, which included a second-tier title win at Molineux, as well as earning 10 England caps.

It is stated that the England Under-21s assistant has already impressed higher-ups at the Football Association after landing mentioned role two months' ago.

Coady terminated his Wrexham contract in August after making just six appearances under Phil Parkinson at the Racecourse Ground, and immediately turned his focus to coaching.

Maxime Esteve made his Champions League debut for RB Leipzig against Lens on Tuesday night, and one of his former teammates was cheering him on.

Sources indicate that one of the biggest costs that comes with relegation from the Premier League can be the loss of players that comes with it. Even relegated sides have some players who will be wanted elsewhere, and many will have clauses in their contracts entitling them to leave in the event that their teams go down by the end of a season.

Industry observers note that this exodus took place at the end of the 2025-26 season for Burnley, just as it routinely does for clubs relegated from this level, and in the case of defender Maxime Esteve the offer was an appealing one. The 24-year-old centre-back signed for RB Leipzig in the summer, and although he's primarily been used as a squad player by the Bundesliga outfit through the opening weeks of this season, he was included in their team for their Champions League match against RC Lens on Tuesday night, his debut in the competition.

Recent findings suggest that it turned out to be a successful night for both the player and his new club. RB Leipzig won the match 3-1, and Esteve scored strongly for his performance before being withdrawn midway through the second half with cramp. And after the match, when he posted to social media about his delight at making his Champions League debut, one of his former Burnley teammates was there in the replies with a show of support for him.

Posting to the social media platform Instagram after RB Leipzig's 3-1 win over RC Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday night, Maxime Esteve couldn't contain his delight at having made his first appearance in Europe's premier club competition, saying, "First Champions League game, at home, and a win to go with it.".

It has been revealed that esteve was clearly very pleased to have been given the opportunity in such a prestigious tournament: "A night I won’t forget. Thanks to the team and to our fans for the atmosphere. Let’s keep going.".

In a recent development, would you have wanted Burnley to keep hold of Maxime Esteve for 2026-27? Let us know in the comments below!

Recent findings suggest that among those congratulating Esteve in the comments was one of his former teammates. Ashley Barnes has played over 300 games for Burnley, but his first spell ended before Esteve arrived at the club. But the former Brighton and Norwich striker returned to the Lancashire club in January 2025 and extended his contract for a year at the end of the 2024-25 season, meaning that the two were in the same Clarets squad for a season and a half.

And it's clear from the reactions to this post - not only from Barnes - but also from a number of Burnley fans, that the central defender is still thought of fondly at Turf Moor, almost half a season on from his departure from their club.

Maxime Esteve's move to RB Leipzig hasn't gone completely according to plan for the 24-year-old defender. He has only made five appearances for his fresh club since arriving in the summer, of which three have been starts. But an assured performance will only have strengthened his case for a more regular berth in their starting eleven.

It has been revealed that this is an exciting time to be at the club. RB Leipzig are in fourth place in the Bundesliga, and although Bayern Munich remain the clear favourites to win the league title, Leipzig are only three points behind current leaders Borussia Dortmund.

It's all a long way removed from Burnley's dismal 2025-26 Premier League season, which ended with the Clarets relegated in 19th place having picked up just 22 points all season, leaving them 19 points short of safety.

In a recent development, ashley Barnes, meanwhile, stayed at Turf Moor following relegation after agreeing another contract extension with Burnley during the summer. But Barnes has not been a central part of the Burnley team since his 2025 return to Turf Moor. He only made seven appearances for them in the Premier League last season, all of which came from the bench and which amounted to just 41 minutes of game time.

This season has seen Barnes get even less game time for Burnley. He has yet to make an appearance for them in the Championship in 2026-27, although at 37 years of age, the striker may be preparing for a post-playing career in coaching rather than being fully focussed on playing. It's already been reported that he'll be joining the club's coaching staff at the end of this season.

The only sighting of him that Burnley fans have had on the pitch this season came with a 45-minute cameo appearance in a Premier League 2 fixture against West Ham United towards the end of October. But the fact that he should be giving such support to one of his former teammates is a positive sign for what Burnley fans can expect from him as a coach.

Paul Merson believes Manchester United must strengthen their defence in January but insists their problems extend beyond the backline, with concerns over their midfield and attacking options also needing attention.

The January transfer window could be the first stop for Pochettino for some shopping but the budget given to him as per a previous report by readmanutd isn’t much to make a difference.

Paul Merson believes the club have several areas to improve rather than focusing only on their defence.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Arsenal midfielder made it clear that United need to bring in defensive reinforcements.

“Manchester United will have to get centre-halves in, defenders in and full-backs in,” Merson stated.

It has been revealed that however, Merson does not believe defensive recruitment alone will solve United’s problems. He also questioned the team’s ability to control games in midfield and expressed concerns about the quality of their attacking options.

“I wouldn’t say that’s just been the problem. I don’t think they’ve got legs in midfield, I don’t think they’re dominating games in midfield,” he explained.

He was also critical of United’s forward line, suggesting that the current attacking options are not consistently performing.

It has been revealed that “I’ve never really been a massive fan of their front three. I think they’re not Manchester United standard, in my opinion.”.

Merson also compared the current generation with some of the club’s former greats, including Wayne Rooney, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Roy Keane, Paul Scholes, David Beckham and Cristiano Ronaldo. He compared players’ consistency with those earlier.

“Back in the day when it’s Rooney and them kind of players and Van Nistelrooy and Keane and Scholes and Beckham and Ronaldo, they were seven, eight out of ten every week. There wasn’t a four out of ten and a nine out of ten.”.

“And if they have a four the week after, it doesn’t really matter. So for me, it hasn’t just been the defence.”.

United could face difficult decisions when the transfer window opens, particularly if they want to strengthen multiple areas of the squad and with the budget available to Pochettino, that doesn’t seem to be the case.

Sources indicate that only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

It has been revealed that but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

According to recent reports, for Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

Sources indicate that the Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews said. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

Recent findings suggest that brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

Recent findings suggest that to play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

Industry observers note that it was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak mentioned. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

Any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very important points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola said they will now be out “for some time”.

The loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

The injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their significant-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa mentioned: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”.

One of the advantages of Iraola’s Anfield appointment was his Premier League experience with Bournemouth. The Basque well knows the division and has plenty of positive memories from which to borrow.

Recent findings suggest that however, there will also be some scar tissue, and that certainly is the case with Brentford. Iraola never beat the Bees in seven attempts (five draws, two defeats), a run which included a 4-1 thrashing at the Gtech Community Stadium in his final season at Bournemouth.

It’s back-to-back wins for Chelsea and a rare clean sheet, their first since January. But all thoughts will be with Emi Martinez after his clash of heads with Branthwaite. Hopefully we get some good news on that front soon. Follow the latest updates here.

Enzo Maresca has been looking for opportunities for rest his key players - but Erling Haaland is a player that is impossible to rest. He has scored in his last seven matches and leads Manchester City’s attack again.

It has been revealed that but Maresca has changed half of his team from the line-up defeated by Paris St-Germain in the week. Jeremy Doku and City’s first-choice centre-backs are the others to keep their place. The rest are drafted in to face Ipswich, with Matheus Nunes, Nico O’Reilly, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Iliman Ndiaye and Mateo Kovačić are drafted in.

There is also a place for Phil Foden after serving his three-match ban for getting dismissed in the Manchester derby.

It has been revealed that keith Andrews has established a clearly defined, direct style of play which speaks to Brentford’s strengths. His side are third in the Premier League for percentage of passes forward (39.2 per cent) and, coupled with the second-most high turnovers which end in a goal, Brentford have thrived off passages of organised chaos.

Industry observers note that to play this way requires quality when you do have the ball, and full-backs Keane Lewis-Potter and Michael Kayode deserve particular praise. They have contributed materially to Brentford’s attacks, helping their side to league-high successful crosses (26) and expected goals from set-pieces (4.03).

Manchester City’s claim to have “irrefutable evidence” that will overturn their guilty verdict on appeal is based on a trove of emails, letters and bank statements.

A re-examination of Abu Dhabi government documents, receipts and testimony from 24 witnesses – all of which the club believe were wrongly dismissed at the original hearing – will be central in attempts to force a full or partial acquittal or retrial, according to people familiar with the case.

Sources with understanding of City’s case have told Telegraph Sport the club are bullish about their appeal, based on:.

Shahid Khan, Fulham’s owner, insists that his team are on a “positive path” despite remaining winless in the Premier League after six matches.

In his programme notes, he wrote: “I want to reflect on our recent form. Prior to the international break, we were trending upward… That momentum carried us through most of Saturday’s match at Ipswich Town, but we all know how that ended. The result was devastating for all of us, and I won’t pretend otherwise.

Industry observers note that “And yet, I am reminded of the positive path we have been on and the genuine potential of this team. Our squad is strong, while still coming together. We have been in every match, missing only the opportunities we’ve had to complete the task. I believe those opportunities will soon be seized.”.

This feels like an extremely treacherous trip for Liverpool and for Andoni Iraola, who has a poor record against Brentford. With Bournemouth, he did not win any of his six matches against today’s opponents.

The good news for Liverpool is that Alexander Isak and Dominik Szoboszlai are fit enough to start the game, and that Brentford top scorer Kevin Schade is not. Schade is on the bench after picking up a shoulder injury against Aston Villa last weekend.

Barcola opened his Liverpool account on Wednesday and he will look to continue his goal-scoring form at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Speaking of the France winger, head coach Andoni Iraola said: “I think it’s still very early, especially for him who hasn’t played any minutes in pre-season, he’s kind of been doing pre-season in the first games with us almost [in] official games.

“It’s remarkable because to score three goals in a Champions League game is … not a lot of players can say they have done it.

“It’s something nice for him but I think the best thing is we can feel him, he seems with confidence on the ball [away] from the goals, straight away you could feel he was confident going in one-to-one situations, attacking the spaces and [those] are his strengths.”.

Industry observers note that good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the 3pm kick-offs. Manchester City burst the Anfield bubble last weekend but were defeated by Paris St-Germain in a Champions League thriller on Wednesday, and Enzo Maresca will have to manage his leading cast members’ workload. Before Ipswich Town’s visit to the Etihad he floated the idea of resting some of his players at some point.

“We are thinking about this not just with Erling [Haaland] because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams,” Maresca stated in his pre-match press conference.”.

“Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernández], Marc [Guéhi], Erling, Rúben [Dias] – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest.”.

Ipswich’s spirited start to the season was characterised by a stunning late turnaround against Fulham last weekend. Gary O’Neil’s side have accrued three wins in their first six top-flight matches for the first time since 1993 and may consider today’s match as something of a free hit.

It has been revealed that elsewhere, Liverpool’s confidence-building midweek win in Austria was underlined by Bradley Barcola’s first, second and third goals for the club. It was exactly what the France winger needed, and with Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo emerging as doubts for this afternoon’s trip to Brentford, the attacking burden may fall on Barcola and Florian Wirtz’s shoulders once more.

Sources indicate that breaking down fourth-placed Brentford, who are one of only three teams to remain undefeated this season, will be a tall task. Keith Andrews’ stock has never been higher, but the same cannot be said for Álvaro Arbeloa, whose winless Fulham are bottom of the league.

Pressure was already mounting before Fulham’s three-game run against the promoted teams, and the late collapse at Portman Road will not have helped the Spaniard’s cause. Defeat by Hull City will not be seen kindly by the club’s hierarchy.

The next wide forward who gets serious minutes at Stamford Bridge has to be assessed against that ceiling, not against the safer language of potential.

Derby County's 3-0 defeat to Wolverhampton Wanderers at Molineux has only increased the speculation over John Eustace's future at Pride Park.

The Rams started off the encounter in encouraging fashion, but, ultimately, could not convert one of their early chances past the experienced Jose Sa.

According to recent reports, eustace's side had returned from the year's final international break with a 2-0 defeat to promotion-chasing Southampton at St. Mary's, and a fourth away defeat in five was confirmed as Cesar Peixoto's outfit turned up the heat with a brace from Adam Armstrong and a merited goal from highly-rated winger, Mateus Mane.

The heavy loss in the West Midlands, coupled with Preston North End's surprise 4-0 rout over Cardiff City in South Wales means that Derby will kickstart the Championship's 17th matchweek at the foot of the table - a far cry from what many predicted was in store for Eustace's side in pre-season.

The experienced head coach has been under pressure for some time, and now scrutiny over his position has reappeared ahead of a must-win encounter against his former club, Watford, on Saturday.

Just last month, Eustace revealed that he retained the full backing of Derby owner, David Clowes, over the potential to turn the club's fortunes around.

Since then, the Rams have accumulated four points from a possible 18, with a sole victory coming through a 3-1 success over Bolton Wanderers on November 6th.

Speaking to local radio post-match, Eustace reaffirmed the confidence he has in himself and his squad to get out of the current situation, but no word has come from the club since the full-time whistle at Molineux, which only increased speculation.

However, BBC Derby Sport's Dominic Dietrich has since confirmed that, as things stand, Eustace will lead the team for Saturday's clash against the Hornets, who, earlier on Wednesday, confirmed Edward Iordanescu as Alessio Dionisi's successor.

For the second time in three seasons, Derby are staring at the prospect of a Championship relegation battle.

Eustace has now lost 36 of his 81 matches in charge, equating in a win ratio of just 36%, and, unsurprisingly, the fresh enhancement has caused a stir.

It has been revealed that one fan commented: "This is quite disrespectful to the fanbase now. Actually not now. But a few games ago. Two possible reasons both really bad. Financial reasons: I can't believe this. Because relegation will be much more expensive. Blind loyalty: Even worse than financial mismanagement.".

"It’s an insult to the fans that there is no official communication from the club," was another response from a displeased Rams follower.

In a recent development, "Simply kicking the can down the road. Irrespective of any result against Watford, it’ll just be papering over the canyon. Fundamental change is needed," stated another supporter.

Echoing such sentiments, one comment read: "Was only last season the chants of 'Eustace barmy army' were loud and proud. Football is a very fickle game. Clowes holding his nerve. Saturday is going to be interesting....".

Rams fans, how much longer can David Clowes afford to stick with John Eustace? Comment below!

Another supporter claimed: "I could understand him keeping his job if we’re losing games by fine margins and they players were all trying but we’ve been utter crap. Wolves had near on 40 shots last night. And his post-match interviews are insane! There is definitely something going on behind the scenes.".

It has been revealed that "How much worse does it need to get? How much worse can it get? 10 points from 51 in this awful league is a disaster," debated another frustrated fan.

Derby are now five points adrift of safety with 29 matches remaining, and whilst that allows plenty of time for the club's fortunes to change, there have been little signs that such feats will occur under Eustace.

The former Birmingham City and Blackburn Rovers boss does have experience of staving off relegation, but, no doubt some of the frustration felt by supporters stems from the actions taken at their relegation rivals.

Preston have taken seven points from their last three matches under Graham Alexander after he replaced Paul Heckingbottom, whilst Burnley, Watford and now Lincoln City have already opted to make managerial changes.

The Rams have won just five league matches since the start of April, and whilst injuries to key men such as Patrick Agyemang haven't helped Eustace, such circumstances were not expected whatsoever.

Therefore, there is plenty of room to improve, and the Bolton boss will know that the cushion to the bottom three can be eaten into very quickly if they don’t keep picking up results.

So, January could be crucial, and one player who is likely to be on the market is Jeremy Monga.

The winger joined Man City from Leicester for around £10m in the summer, and he was immediately loaned to Swansea, which seemed like a good fit for the player.

However, with Moussa Yeo, Elijah Just and Joseph Opoku also joining the Welsh club in the summer, it’s fair to say competition for places is fierce in the final third.

The past few months will be hugely frustrating for Monga, and video footage of the player wandering around the pitch on his own after the recent game against West Brom left many feeling sorry for the 17-year-old, who has seen his career stall.

As a result, it’s fair to say that Monga and his parent club will be counting down the days until the January window opens, so his season-long loan can be cut short.

Of course, Vitor Matos’ departure from Swansea could change things, but the Welsh club are stacked for talent in the final third.

Elijah Just, Moussa Yeo and Joseph Opoku were among the summer additions, so game time was always going to be difficult to come by for Monga, and it’s hard to envisage him forcing his way into the XI even under a latest head coach.

Following on from that, if City do send Monga somewhere else, they will be prioritising first-team football for the player, which could make Bolton the perfect fit.

Right now, the likes of Thierry Gale, Samuel Iling-Junior and Kylian Dong have all struggled for form, even if Gale has made some decent contributions earlier on in the campaign.

Nevertheless, attacking reinforcements will be the priority, and Monga could flourish in Schumacher’s setup.

Unlike many newly-promoted teams, Bolton are a front-footed, attacking team, and they haven’t been scared of taking the game to their opponents - as the likes of West Ham and Wolves found out, even if they did ultimately lose against the Hammers.

As part of his XI, Schumacher wants wingers who can hug the touchline, and he gives them freedom to carry the ball and express themselves.

That’s exactly what Monga needs right now, and, despite his age, the England youth international proved on occasions with Leicester last season that he can cause problems at this level.

We know that Bolton don’t have the biggest budget in the Championship, so they have to be smart in their recruitment, and they have made some good signings in the past few windows.

But, January is also difficult, and you don’t want to get sucked into paying over the odds for players, so it’s all about finding the balance.

Where will Bolton finish in the Championship this season? Let us know in the comments below.

In Monga, Bolton could get an exciting talent on loan, and, if it does work out, it will only enhance their reputation for developing players, which could be crucial moving forward.

So, it’s certainly one that they should pursue, and January will be a massive month for the Trotters if they want to ensure they can have a comfortable end to the campaign.

Unbeaten record on the line: All the key stats ahead of Milan vs. Frosinone

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan and Frosinone will meet for the only the seventh time this evening at San Siro, with a dominant record to try uphold.

Industry observers note that the Rossoneri have certainly enjoyed a better run of things in this fixture, with four wins and two draws so far. They have won the last three as well, spread across the 2023-24 and 2018-19 seasons, outside of which Frosinone were in Serie B.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Sources indicate that in the most recent meeting, Olivier Giroud opened the scoring for Milan away from home but then the hosts scored twice. However, Matteo Gabbia and Luka Jovic both scored as the Diavolo were able to come from behind and win.

In a recent development, the most recent game at San Siro was a 3-1 win for Milan as Jovic, Christian Pulisic and Fikayo Tomori found the back of the net. Given that Frosinone are the surprise package of the season so far, tonight could be a much tougher test.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in all six previous meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W4 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

In a recent development, ➤ Milan have scored at least three goals in four of their six Serie A matches against Frosinone, producing 15 goals overall, an average of 2.5 per game. Only against Pescara (2.9) have they recorded a higher average, among the opponents they have faced on at least five occasions (2.5 also against Casale and Messina).

➤ Frosinone have won six games this season, drawing two and losing three. Only three newly promoted teams in the last 40 years have recorded more wins in their first 12 Serie A games of the season: Bari in 1994/95 (seven), Chievo in 2001/02 (seven), and Hellas Verona in 2013/14 (seven).

➤ Milan have won four of their last five league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in consecutive Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

➤ Although Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their five away games this season (W1 D2), they have won just two of their last 27 away games in Serie A (including previous participations), with 10 draws and 15 defeats.

Sources indicate that ➤ Milan have failed to win four of their last seven Serie A games played after the international break (D2 L2). On the other hand, Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their last five top-flight matches immediately following Italy matches (W2 D1).

➤ Frosinone have attempted the most counterattacks from advantageous situations in Serie A this season: 22, almost double the number of any other team. On the other hand, Milan are the only team that haven’t allowed a single counterattack when trailing in the current campaign.

It has been revealed that ➤ Only Juventus (79) have attempted more long-range shots than Frosinone (77) this season. On the other hand, Milan are the team that have attempted the fewest shots from outside the area (30) and the one that have conceded the most shots from outside the area in relation to the total conceded, 44%.

➤ Adrien Rabiot has earned the most points for his team from direct goal contributions this season, having scored 10 goals and assisted four times. In the most recent matchday, he became the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal in six consecutive league appearances since Kaká in 2004 (who managed seven).

➤ Only Matías Soulé (80) has been involved in more sequences ending with a shot than Giacomo Calò (76) in this Serie A. The Frosinone player has scored five goals in the current campaign and only one midfielder has scored more goals in the first 12 matchdays in the top flight for a newly promoted team in the three points for a win era: Hidetoshi Nakata with Perugia in 1998/99 (six).
